This is Drop Site Daily, our free news recap We send it Monday - Friday Iran Iran destroys U.S. early warning radar in Bahrain, IRGC says: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) that it destroyed a U.S. early warning radar system in Bahrain in response to an attack on a telecommunications tower in the southern Iranian port of Sirik on Thursday. Bahrain is home to the U.S. Navy's 5th Fleet. It is the first Iranian attack on Bahrain since September. "This serves as a serious warning to the aggressor enemy to cease its aerial provocations and oil smuggling in the Strait of Hormuz. Should these violations and acts of aggression recur, the IRGC Aerospace Force stands in full readiness to engage without limits," the IRGC said. Iran's navy also said that it shot down an U.S. MQ-1 Predator drone over the Strait of Hormuz, the state-aligned Islamic Republic News Agency reported. The drone was downed on the southern Sirik coast. Another tanker hits mine in Hormuz, IRGC says: A liquefied petroleum gas tanker struck a mine in the Strait of Hormuz, causing an explosion, the IRGC said, adding that the Iranian navy sent repeated warnings against using an "unauthorized" south passage through the strait. Iran tells UN nuclear agency inspections cannot proceed while under threat from U.S.: Iran told the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) this month that discussions on nuclear monitoring cannot proceed while it is under threat from military attacks, the Associated Press , citing a confidential report by the IAEA circulated to member states on Friday. Iran said that discussions on nuclear inspections cannot resume amid "a series of persistent, explicit, and public threats by the President of the United States of America . . . to commit further acts of armed aggression" against Iran, "particularly targeting its nuclear facilities." In a letter to the IAEA, Iran expressed concern about the U.S. State Department's recent announcement that it would pay up to $20 million for information on Iran's nuclear program. Iran has not granted IAEA inspectors access to nuclear sites targeted by Israel and the U.S. during the 12-day war in June 2025. The IAEA expressed "increasing concern" about a fuel enrichment plant in Isfahan. Inspectors were due to visit the facility on the day the U.S.-Israeli strikes began in June, but cancelled the inspection. The IAEA said in its report that it "does not know" the site's "exact location or whether it contains nuclear material." IEA: Global oil market returning to surplus: The global oil market will return to a surplus in the fourth quarter of 2026, the International Energy Agency (IEA) said in its monthly oil. Exports from the Middle East are recovering despite continued attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. "The oil market is showing tentative signs of rebalancing, with global oil supplies surpassing demand for the first time since the outbreak of the war in Iran," the IEA said. Palestine Israeli military shoots and kills Palestinian in Gaza City: A Palestinian was killed by Israeli gunfire in the Tuffah neighborhood of Gaza City on Friday morning, according to Al Jazeera. 49 countries call on Israel to allow humanitarian aid into Gaza: On Thursday, 49 countries issued a joint urging Israel to ease its restrictions on aid, warning that its near-total blockade was worsening public-health conditions in Gaza. The signatories called on Israel to allow aid to enter Gaza unhindered, demanding that it reopen humanitarian corridors and approve essential supplies, including so-called "dual-use items" that Israel bans from entering Gaza. "As winter sets in, far too many people in Gaza are still without adequate shelter, and risk exposure to hypothermia, respiratory infections, waterborne diseases and other preventable illnesses," Britain's ambassador to the United Nations, Sarah MacIntosh, said at the UN headquarters in New York on Thursday. The appeal specifically emphasized supplies needed for shelter, fuel, water, sanitation, and medical care. It also called on Israel to allow medical patients in Gaza to receive care in East Jerusalem and the West Bank. The countries also noted that medical and humanitarian workers and facilities must be protected, urged expedited criminal investigations into Israeli attacks on medical personnel, and demanded that Israel grant senior international delegations and journalists access to Gaza. The initiative was led by Britain, Qatar, and Jordan and backed by countries including Australia, Canada, Egypt, France, Italy, the Netherlands, Poland, Saudi Arabia, Spain, and Turkey. The United States did not sign the statement. Israeli forces conduct raids, arrest Palestinians across occupied West Bank: Israeli forces conducted raids and arrested Palestinians across the occupied West Bank on Friday, WAFA . Israeli soldiers arrested four Palestinians in towns around the city of Jenin. Troops stormed the town of Al-Ubeidiya, east of Bethlehem, firing sound bombs and taking up positions in the town. They raided several neighborhoods in Nablus, and searched homes in the nearby towns of Beit Furik and Beit Dajan. The Israeli army invaded the village of Marda, north of Salfit, with soldiers searching a large number of homes, detaining a number of young men, and subjecting them to field interrogations before releasing them. Yemen Saudi-led coalition kills five civilians in Saada: Shelling by the Saudi-led coalition in the northern governorate of Saada killed five civilians on Friday, Al Jazeera reported. Ansarallah carried out raids on sites in Taiz and attacked government military camps with six ballistic missiles, Al Jazeera reported, citing Ansarallah sources. Airlines extend suspension of flights to Saudi Arabia amid continued Ansarallah attacks: International airlines extended flight suspensions to several cities in Saudi Arabia as Ansarallah targets airports, energy facilities, and infrastructure in missile and drone attacks. Several Indian airlines announced that flights to Saudi cities including Riyadh, Jeddah, Dammam, and Medina would remain suspended until late November. Emirati and Omani carriers announced similar extensions. KLM has cancelled service to late November while British Airways postponed the resumption of its London-Riyadh route until January 2027. Lebanon Israel attacks southern Lebanon, again violating so-called ceasefire: The Israeli military shelled several towns in southern Lebanon on Friday, the Lebanese government-aligned National News Agency reported. Among the towns Israel attacked were Mayfadoun, Talloussah, and Bani Haiyyan. No casualties were reported. U.S. News Sen. Chris Van Hollen announces he will run for Senate majority leader: Maryland Democratic Sen. Chris Van Hollen that he will challenge Sen. Chuck Schumer (D-N.Y.) for Senate majority leader. In an announcement on Thursday, Van Hollen said that "the American people called for change" in the midterms, adding that the Democratic Party "needs new leadership." He said that if he was elected, he would use every tool available to the majority to end the Iran War, including leveraging a December funding deadline. Sen. Bernie Sanders (I-Vt.) and Sen.-elect Abdul El-Sayed (D-Mich.) endorsed him after his announcement, while Sens. Angus King (I-Maine) and Kirsten Gillibrand (D-N.Y.) criticized Van Hollen's challenge and defended Schumer as an architect of sweeping Democratic wins in the midterms. Congressional Democrats will choose their leaders in a closed-door caucus in December. To become the party's majority leader, Schumer or Van Hollen will need the support of 28 of the party's 55 Senators. Keep track of where senators stand on the leadership vote with . CBS: ICE deported a record 483,200 people in 2026: Immigration and Customs Enforcement a record 483,200 people in fiscal year 2026, according to Homeland Security data obtained by CBS. The total tops the prior record of 442,640 ICE deportees in the 2025 fiscal year. The nonpartisan Migration Policy Institute found that only about 20% of roughly 980,000 ICE and CBP deportees since January 2025 had ever been convicted of a crime. Exit polls from the midterm elections showed that voters rejected the Trump administration's far-right immigration policies. Peltola maintains lead over Sullivan in Alaska 's Senate race: As of Friday morning,** Democratic Senate nominee Mary Peltola Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan by 3,975 votes in Alaska's Senate race, which has not been called. According to data from Decision Desk HQ, Peltola has received over 48.5% of votes, and Sullivan has received over 46.9%. Tens of thousands of ballots from Anchorage and other rural areas have yet to be counted. Politico: Mamdani plans to disband the NYPD 's protest unit: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani plans to the New York Police Department's Strategic Response Group, a controversial crowd-control unit that has repeatedly cracked down on nonviolent protesters, Politico reported. A formal announcement is expected as early as next week. Civil-rights advocates and activists have accused the police unit of excessive force and misconduct. NYPD Commissioner Jessica Tisch has supported keeping the SRG unit. Trump urges Senate Republicans to pass $350 billion in defense spending: On Thursday, President Donald Trump that Republican legislators must pass a new $350 billion in defense spending before losing their Congressional majority. "Republicans must deliver for our Warriors. The Democrats never will. The time is NOW," Trump on Truth Social on Thursday. A budget outlined passed by the House includes Iran war funding, but it has stalled in the Senate for almost four months. The budget outline provides $60 billion for the Pentagon. Donald Trump Jr. leaves advisory role at prediction market Kalshi: Donald Trump Jr. is his advisory role at the prediction market Kalshi, Bloomberg reported. A Kalshi spokesperson said that Trump Jr. and Kalshia "mutually agreed to end Don's advisory role after his firm's significant investment in a competitor this past summer," a reference to his firm 1789 Capital's stake in the rival prediction company Polymarket, where he is also an adviser. Families of U.S. Navy sailors told to prepare for 12-month deployment: At a November 9 town hall, Navy leaders that the USS George H.W. Bush aircraft carrier will not be home for the holidays. Acting Secretary of the Navy Hung Cao told families at the town hall that the soldiers would return home when there is a "non-nuclear Iran." The carrier left Naval Station Norfolk, in Virginia, for the Middle East on March 31. At the time, its deployment was expected to last six or seven months. The Navy said that War Secretary Pete Hegseth would decide when to bring the carrier home from the Middle East. Trump says possibility of U.S. military operation against Cuba "before I leave": Asked on Thursday about a military operation against Cuba, President Trump , "I would like to be able to do it," adding that he wants to "get Cuba done before I leave." Trump said that Secretary of State Marco Rubio was the administration's leader on the issue. Earlier this week, Trump told reporters at the White House that the Cuban government would fall "very soon," and last week at Mar-a-Lago he said that Rubio was "going to work on Cuba." 📥 Have a tip on Capitol Hill? Email DC Correspondent Julian Andreone at Julian@dropsitenews.com. Other International News Exclusive: Al-Shabaab ambushes U.S.-trained Somali special forces: Al-Shabaab fighters ambushed U.S.-trained Somali forces near the town of Yaqbirweyne, in the volatile Lower Shabelle region, on Thursday, Drop Site News contributor Mohamed Gabobe reports. A five-vehicle convoy of Danab ("Lightning") Brigade forces was ambushed during a routine patrol, two Somali security officials told Drop Site. The Danab is an elite indigenous counter-terrorism force that the U.S. helped create during the second administration of Barack Obama. It is explicitly tasked with fighting Al-Shabaab. Eight soldiers were killed in the fighting, the officials said, and Al-Shabaab seized two of the convoy's vehicles. The militant group claimed to have killed 17 Danab troops. According to the Somali Ministry of Defense, two high-ranking field commanders were among the dead. The ambush occurred near a recently abandoned U.S. military base, the Baledogle Airfield, that is about 60 miles from Mogadishu, the capital of Somalia. Earlier this month, the U.S. confirmed its withdrawal from the base. "The relocation from Baledogle was 100% an economic decision," Army Lt. Gen. John Brennan, deputy commander of the U.S. military's Africa command, this month. "The surface of the airfield was declining to the point where it was becoming dangerous to land aircraft there." Baledogle was the largest U.S. military base in Somalia. In September, Mohamed Gabobe reported in Drop Site News that the U.S. military is constructing a new base in Bosaso, Somalia, a port city on the shores of the Gulf of Aden. Read the full story. Imran Khan 's sisters released from prison: Uzma Khan and Noreen Niazi Khan, two sisters of former Pakistani Prime Minister Imran Khan, were from prison after 53 days, their lawyer said on Thursday. Their third sister, Aleema Khan, remains in prison. The three sisters were arrested a week before a planned September 27 march demanding the release of their brother Imran Khan, who has been imprisoned since August 2023. The march, organized by his Pakistan Tehreek-i-Insaf Party (PTI), was canceled after the federal government suspended the PTI-led government in the province of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. Last month, Drop Site contributor Mehr Sher reported on the Pakistani government's violent crackdown in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. Read the full story. Pakistani police and Taliban exchange fire; 10 officers, up to 18 Taliban fighters dead: Pakistani Taliban fighters police officers in the Kohat area of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan, on Thursday. Ten police officers and 18 Taliban gunmen were killed, according to provincial police, and 12 police officers were wounded. The attack occurred as police officers were returning from a mine in the Gumbat area on Wednesday. U.S. State Department releases report on whereabouts of $12 billion taken from Venezuela: On Thursday, the State Department a 53-page report outlining the U.S. government's disbursement of over $12 billion in oil and mineral revenue that it has seized from Venezuela since U.S. forces abducted President Nicolas Maduro in January. Of the total sum seized, $169 million remains unaccounted for. The State Department report is heavily redacted, and the identities of many relevant parties to the transactions are unknown. According to the report, as of September almost all of the seized funds were sent to Venezuelan banks, which used foreign-currency exchanges to prop up the Venezuelan bolivar, the country's currency. Russian court sentences rights lawyer for treason: On Thursday, a court in the Russian exclave of Kaliningrad Maria Bontsler, a 66-year-old rights lawyer, to 12 years in prison, plus a year of "restrictions" on her freedom, for treason. Prosecutors accused her of relaying information about criminal cases in Kaliningrad to Ukraine. The rights group Slovo Zashchite said that Bontsler had defended several defendants in political cases, and that her trial was held behind closed doors. Bontsler and her lawyers were barred from attending the trial, the group added, and their participation was limited to presenting a closing statement. Russian courts have previously imprisoned lawyers who take politically sensitive cases, as in the 2025 cases of three lawyers who represented the opposition leader Alexey Navalny, who was killed by poisoning in 2024. Russian soldier killed in St. Petersburg car-bombing: A Russian soldier was after the SUV he was driving exploded in St. Petersburg, Russia, Reuters reported. Russian police are investigating the killing as a murder. The Russian newspaper Fontanka reported that a 31-year-old suspect planted the bomb under the car of the soldier, said to be a colonel, after conducting at least a month of surveillance. The suspect has fled the country, according to the paper. In August, a Russian serviceman died in a car explosion in St. Petersburg. Italian schools mostly stay open despite second day of hoax bomb threats : More than 3,700 Italian schools bomb threats on Thursday, but only 77 schools were evacuated, after Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni said that only the threats with "concrete elements beyond the mere receipt of a mass email" should be taken seriously. About 6,300 schools received bomb threats on Wednesday. The emails were signed by "Mikhail Andropov," and threatened Meloni herself. Schools in Scotland, Northern Ireland, and Ireland received similar emails but remained in session. Indonesian vice president resigns; wiretapping investigation ongoing: Indonesia's Vice President, Gibran Rakabuming Raka, stepped down on Thursday. He said that he resigned to avoid a prolonged political controversy, though a cabinet minister present at a meeting where his resignation was discussed said that President Prabowo Subianto urged Gibran to defend himself. Separately on Thursday, Indonesian police announced that they gathered enough initial evidence to pursue treason charges against four suspects accused of wiretapping Prabowo. Former police chief Listyo Sigit Prabowo (of no relation to the president) and three senior police officials were arrested last week over suspicion that they monitored phones belonging to President Prabowo, other government officials, activists, and journalists. Listyo Prabowo was a close advisor to President Prabowo. Former senior Bolivian judge arrested on suspicion of drug trafficking: On Wednesday, Bolivian authorities Aldo Quezada, the former chief justice of the Santa Cruz departmental court, on suspicion of drug trafficking. He resigned last month after the U.S. restricted his visa over alleged links to drug traffickers. The U.S. government's visa-restrictions list has also targeted officials in Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru. Quezada is one of several senior Bolivian judicial officials arrested since September. Former Attorney General Roger Mariaca was arrested on September 30 on suspicion of money laundering and drug trafficking. Right-wing President Rodrigo Paz, who took office in November 2025, has sought closer ties with the U.S. Last month, Drop Site's Jose Luis Granada Ceja reported on the arrest of Mariaca and the selective use of drug-trafficking accusations to advance U.S. interests in Latin America. Read the full story. Sudanese military leader meets with heads of state from Turkey, Pakistan, and Libya at climate summit: Sudanese army chief Abdel Fattah al-Burhan with Turkish President Recep Erdogan, Pakistani President Shehbaz Sharif, and Libyan Prime Minister Abdulhamid Dbeibah on the sidelines of the COP31 climate summit in Turkey on Thursday. Al-Burhan's office said that the meetings focused on political and security issues in Sudan and diplomatic and economic relations among the countries. UN peacekeepers, South Sudanese authorities failed to prevent massacre in South Sudanese village, Amnesty says: The UN Mission in South Sudan (UNMISS) was about a March 2026 attack in Abiemnom, South Sudan, but did not reinforce its peacekeeping ranks until after the attack, Amnesty International said in a report on Thursday. As many as 1,500 armed men attacked the village of Abiemnom, shooting residents, burning more than 230 structures, and looting a hospital. More than 200 people died. After Amnesty released the report, a UNMISS spokesperson said that cuts to the UN peacekeeping force's budget required the force to concentrate on protecting about 2,500 people sheltering at its base. The spokesperson said that UNMISS repeatedly asked the South Sudanese army for more forces. subject: Let me tell it to you straight

body:
We won because of you | | | | The stakes could not have been higher, Derek, and you showed up. It’s Gov. Tony Evers, and I gotta tell you, I was optimistic heading into Election Day, but I could never have expected these results. David Crowley defeated Tom Tiffany handily, even though David was outspent 2.5 to 1 by Tiffany’s billionaire backers. **And to add a cherry on top, Democrats took back both houses of the State Legislature, giving us a Democratic trifecta in Madison for the first time in years!** Derek, there are going to be a lot of pundits talking out of their you-know-where about how Democrats were able to pull off such an amazing victory. But they don’t know Wisconsin. So let me tell you how we won: 🔵 **It took unity**. That is why Democrats went on a 19-stop Unity Tour across the state – because we are all Democrats, **_and we are all in this to win_**. 🟢 **It took teamwork, and lots of it**. From knocking doors to making phone calls, volunteers outworked MAGA Republicans to get the job done. 🟡 **And it took you, Derek. Yes, you!** Every donation, big or small, was essential to electing David Crowley and Democrats up and down the ballot. This is how we won, and if Democrats continue to follow this playbook, we will keep winning in Wisconsin and across the country. But, Derek, far-right extremists aren’t going to stop attacking Wisconsin just because they got their tuchuses handed to them. [**That is why Democrats must keep investing in Wisconsin, and I’m asking you to chip in now to keep these wins going. body:
I promise I won’t take up much of your time.

*https://secure.anedot.com/stand-in-the-gap/pa-action?utm_campaign=20261113&utm;_content=rtf* | | | [View this email in your browser](*|ARCHIVE|*)
---
| | [](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckD1uxCAUhE-DO1v8eP1TUERaudu0KdEzPNsoGBC83Vw_8kq5QNqZ0eib-XqYB_jg4_4JJ-pCmynVDLyiTdFVSpUgOh_pwB2ykVwOrRCtUAYs-ReaHhqnnXUgbINajHN_m8b-NjeHBslXyzcxWhBqHGFdp2mae2X7Ca3k0Hh99QkhlBgUv43dNDmUgM7xbZ35vLKeQ8BCXcH8XIO3EAnq95aKxc6mswn6IMqVqQ8mFyaXivZZsIOILtGVuLRrQetjSwe2O2QmlwzthZ8iU8uTTmPhzOD3yNT9j4jJ4e2kSBiJqXuhrSna5R8fgq_DyHq-n-DDm4P-99xLy98AAAD__1eEfq4)
Friend,

I promise I won’t take up much of your time.

My name is Shane Jenkins, and I founded Stand In The Gap Foundation. As one of the January 6 defendants, I watched what my fellow patriots endured: arrests, relentless transfers between facilities, prolonged solitary confinement, and families left to face the full weight of the government alone.

**Our nation’s justice system is being weaponized against ordinary Americans.** That’s why we exist: to stand in the gap for Americans facing judicial injustice, so no one has to fight the system by themselves.

Today, especially in the next sixty minutes, I want to reach as many people as I can with this request. I’ve set a goal to raise $20,000 before the end of the month to support our four initiatives under Operation Restore.

**If that is all you need to hear, please contribute $10 or whatever you can afford using this button:**
[Support Stand In The Gap Foundation](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckD1uxCAUhE-DO1v8eP1TUERaudu0KdEzPNsoGBC83Vw_8kq5QNqZ0eib-XqYB_jg4_4JJ-pCmynVDLyiTdFVSpUgOh_pwB2ykVwOrRCtUAYs-ReaHhqnnXUgbINajHN_m8b-NjeHBslXyzcxWhBqHGFdp2mae2X7Ca3k0Hh99QkhlBgUv43dNDmUgM7xbZ35vLKeQ8BCXcH8XIO3EAnq95aKxc6mswn6IMqVqQ8mFyaXivZZsIOILtGVuLRrQetjSwe2O2QmlwzthZ8iU8uTTmPhzOD3yNT9j4jJ4e2kSBiJqXuhrSna5R8fgq_DyHq-n-DDm4P-99xLy98AAAD__1eEfq4)
**Otherwise, let me explain why I’m asking you to give at least $10 to our four initiatives:**

[$10 because Stand for Justice](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckD1uxCAUhE-DO1v8eP1TUERaudu0KdEzPNsoGBC83Vw_8kq5QNqZ0eib-XqYB_jg4_4JJ-pCmynVDLyiTdFVSpUgOh_pwB2ykVwOrRCtUAYs-ReaHhqnnXUgbINajHN_m8b-NjeHBslXyzcxWhBqHGFdp2mae2X7Ca3k0Hh99QkhlBgUv43dNDmUgM7xbZ35vLKeQ8BCXcH8XIO3EAnq95aKxc6mswn6IMqVqQ8mFyaXivZZsIOILtGVuLRrQetjSwe2O2QmlwzthZ8iU8uTTmPhzOD3yNT9j4jJ4e2kSBiJqXuhrSna5R8fgq_DyHq-n-DDm4P-99xLy98AAAD__1eEfq4) provides legal defense, hardship relief, and record sealing for January 6 defendants and others prosecuted for who they are rather than what they did.

[$10 because Bring My Baby Home](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckD1uxCAUhE-DO1v8eP1TUERaudu0KdEzPNsoGBC83Vw_8kq5QNqZ0eib-XqYB_jg4_4JJ-pCmynVDLyiTdFVSpUgOh_pwB2ykVwOrRCtUAYs-ReaHhqnnXUgbINajHN_m8b-NjeHBslXyzcxWhBqHGFdp2mae2X7Ca3k0Hh99QkhlBgUv43dNDmUgM7xbZ35vLKeQ8BCXcH8XIO3EAnq95aKxc6mswn6IMqVqQ8mFyaXivZZsIOILtGVuLRrQetjSwe2O2QmlwzthZ8iU8uTTmPhzOD3yNT9j4jJ4e2kSBiJqXuhrSna5R8fgq_DyHq-n-DDm4P-99xLy98AAAD__1eEfq4) helps parents fight to bring home children taken by a system that never should have taken them in the first place.

[$10 because Restore Honor](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckD1uxCAUhE-DO1v8eP1TUERaudu0KdEzPNsoGBC83Vw_8kq5QNqZ0eib-XqYB_jg4_4JJ-pCmynVDLyiTdFVSpUgOh_pwB2ykVwOrRCtUAYs-ReaHhqnnXUgbINajHN_m8b-NjeHBslXyzcxWhBqHGFdp2mae2X7Ca3k0Hh99QkhlBgUv43dNDmUgM7xbZ35vLKeQ8BCXcH8XIO3EAnq95aKxc6mswn6IMqVqQ8mFyaXivZZsIOILtGVuLRrQetjSwe2O2QmlwzthZ8iU8uTTmPhzOD3yNT9j4jJ4e2kSBiJqXuhrSna5R8fgq_DyHq-n-DDm4P-99xLy98AAAD__1eEfq4) protects service members who were unjustly punished by the very system they swore to defend.

[$10 because Protect Freedom](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckD1uxCAUhE-DO1v8eP1TUERaudu0KdEzPNsoGBC83Vw_8kq5QNqZ0eib-XqYB_jg4_4JJ-pCmynVDLyiTdFVSpUgOh_pwB2ykVwOrRCtUAYs-ReaHhqnnXUgbINajHN_m8b-NjeHBslXyzcxWhBqHGFdp2mae2X7Ca3k0Hh99QkhlBgUv43dNDmUgM7xbZ35vLKeQ8BCXcH8XIO3EAnq95aKxc6mswn6IMqVqQ8mFyaXivZZsIOILtGVuLRrQetjSwe2O2QmlwzthZ8iU8uTTmPhzOD3yNT9j4jJ4e2kSBiJqXuhrSna5R8fgq_DyHq-n-DDm4P-99xLy98AAAD__1eEfq4) helps seniors and vulnerable adults stripped of their rights by the courts that were meant to protect them.

Different courtrooms, same pattern: an ordinary American up against the full weight of the state, with nobody standing beside them. Donations from people like you change that.

**When a family walks into that courtroom with someone in their corner, know it was your support today that made the difference.**

[Can I count on you to contribute $10, or whatever you can afford today, to help us stand beside more Americans facing a weaponized justice system? Click any button below to give today.](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckD1uxCAUhE-DO1v8eP1TUERaudu0KdEzPNsoGBC83Vw_8kq5QNqZ0eib-XqYB_jg4_4JJ-pCmynVDLyiTdFVSpUgOh_pwB2ykVwOrRCtUAYs-ReaHhqnnXUgbINajHN_m8b-NjeHBslXyzcxWhBqHGFdp2mae2X7Ca3k0Hh99QkhlBgUv43dNDmUgM7xbZ35vLKeQ8BCXcH8XIO3EAnq95aKxc6mswn6IMqVqQ8mFyaXivZZsIOILtGVuLRrQetjSwe2O2QmlwzthZ8iU8uTTmPhzOD3yNT9j4jJ4e2kSBiJqXuhrSna5R8fgq_DyHq-n-DDm4P-99xLy98AAAD__1eEfq4)

clean_body: I promise I won’t take up much of your time. | | | |ARCHIVE| | | Friend, I promise I won’t take up much of your time. My name is Shane Jenkins, and I founded Stand In The Gap Foundation. As one of the January 6 defendants, I watched what my fellow patriots endured: arrests, relentless transfers between facilities, prolonged solitary confinement, and families left to face the full weight of the government alone. Our nation’s justice system is being weaponized against ordinary Americans. That’s why we exist: to stand in the gap for Americans facing judicial injustice, so no one has to fight the system by themselves. Today, especially in the next sixty minutes, I want to reach as many people as I can with this request. I’ve set a goal to raise $20,000 before the end of the month to support our four initiatives under Operation Restore. If that is all you need to hear, please contribute $10 or whatever you can afford using this button: Otherwise, let me explain why I’m asking you to give at least $10 to our four initiatives: provides legal defense, hardship relief, and record sealing for January 6 defendants and others prosecuted for who they are rather than what they did. helps parents fight to bring home children taken by a system that never should have taken them in the first place. protects service members who were unjustly punished by the very system they swore to defend. helps seniors and vulnerable adults stripped of their rights by the courts that were meant to protect them. Different courtrooms, same pattern: an ordinary American up against the full weight of the state, with nobody standing beside them. Donations from people like you change that. When a family walks into that courtroom with someone in their corner, know it was your support today that made the difference. Thank you for standing in the gap, Shane Jenkins Co-founder & Initiative Coordinator Stand In The Gap Foundation P.S. | | Has it sunk in yet, team? **The American people have delivered a thorough, historic rejection of MAGA authoritarianism and Republican extremism.** You should be proud of everything you did to help make sure more voters could make their voices heard — in the face of ruthless, racist map-rigging and voter suppression attempts. Thank you for your dedication to democracy as a member of the Fair Fight team. Alongside supporters, donors, and volunteers from across the country, you helped deliver sweeping victories up and down the ballot. These wins were years in the making. Since our founding after the 2018 elections, Fair Fight has pushed back against Jim Crow-style voter suppression, worked to elect Democracy Champions, and pursued the fundamental principle of equal access to the ballot box. It’s paid off. Activists like you shocked the political world by helping elect Mississippi’s first Democratic Senator in decades and first Black U.S. Senator since Reconstruction. You’ve also continued to prove that in Georgia, when we lock arms and fight side by side, we can win big. Keisha Lance Bottoms will be our next governor, flipping the seat from red to blue and becoming the first Black woman to run any state in the nation. Jon Ossoff will return to the U.S. Senate, where he will continue fighting for nationwide pro-democracy reforms and voting rights protections. Democrats swept statewide offices in Georgia. And Georgia Democrats flipped the State House for the first time in decades. We’ve believed this was possible for a long time. In 2011, Stacey Abrams became House minority leader as Republicans rigged the voting maps to try and lock in a supermajority. But, they never got it. Between 2014 and 2020, Democrats brought 800,000 new Georgians into the process. In 2018, they won 11 House seats, then gained more in every election since. This year, Fair Fight went all in with Georgia Takes the House, working alongside a strong coalition and the candidates, volunteers, grassroots donors, and voters who made this happen. Now Republicans won’t be able to redraw Georgia’s maps on their own, and Leader Carolyn Hugley is in line to become Georgia’s first Black woman Speaker. **Georgia doesn’t wait for the odds to change. We change them.** The results prove the power of a basic formula: investing in long-term organizing to expand the electorate and protect the freedom to vote. There was a time when you’d get laughed out of the room if you said Georgia would be a battleground state. (Ask me how I know.) Now it’s undeniable. **And now we can continue to apply that same formula across the South** — pressing our advantage in states that are suddenly swinging blue in the heart of the Old Confederacy, despite all the Neo-Confederate attempts to suppress Black and brown voters and cement white, one-party rule. Look at Mississippi. Look at Texas. Look at South Carolina. Look at Louisiana, Alabama, Tennessee, and Florida, where Democrats came within just a few points of victory. **The numbers are there. The commitment is there — from tireless organizers who continue to build on the legacy of generations of freedom fighters. Together, we’ll keep fighting to make sure no one counts out the South.** Now let’s march forward. Thank you, Lauren Groh-Wargo

body:
The Work We're Proud Of: Spots and Mailers from the 2026 Cycle. | | | |
---
| | |
#### ** Everything is Bigger in Texas,
Even Election History**
---
|
---
| Friends,

This cycle, we had the privilege of bringing candidates’ messages to life in English and Spanish—connecting the economic pressures families face with the failures of Republican leadership and a clear alternative. Here are a few examples of creative that broke through:
**Texas Governor: Gina Hinojosa**
In "No Te Dejes," produced for Somos PAC, we spoke directly to Texas families facing rising energy costs while Greg Abbott handed billions in tax incentives to data centers.
---
| [ ](https://us.list-manage.com/NrBnPks2dbV?e=b8f90417f9&c2id=150df94da93954b2128cfda2414939d1)
---
**"No Te Dejes," ran by Somos PAC**
| **TX-15: Bobby Pulido**
These ads held Monica De La Cruz accountable for supporting a budget that cut Medicaid in one of the nation’s poorest districts, while showing why Texans need a fighter like Bobby Pulido.
---
| [ ](https://us.list-manage.com/vIcNmdyablD?e=b8f90417f9&c2id=150df94da93954b2128cfda2414939d1)
---
**_Nunca_ ran by House Majority PAC**
[ ](https://us.list-manage.com/KUOsPYfX23u?e=b8f90417f9&c2id=150df94da93954b2128cfda2414939d1)
---
**_Luchara_ ran by SOMOS PAC**
| **CO-08: Manny Rutinel**
Our digital ads and DCCC mailer put Manny Rutinel’s record side by side with Gabe Evans’s votes supporting Trump’s Iran war while diesel prices topped $6 a gallon in Colorado.
---
| [ ](https://us.list-manage.com/Lqe3jix57Y2?e=b8f90417f9&c2id=150df94da93954b2128cfda2414939d1)
---
**_El Rey_ ran by House Majority PAC**
[ ](https://us.list-manage.com/TbZBAcrXu96?e=b8f90417f9&c2id=150df94da93954b2128cfda2414939d1)
---
**Mailer ran by the DCCC**
| **AZ-06: JoAnna Mendoza**
In “Elegimos,” produced for House Majority PAC, and in a mailer for Unidos Action Fund, we highlighted Juan Ciscomani’s broken promises and how his votes on tariffs and health care left Arizonans footing the bill.
---
| [ ](https://us.list-manage.com/BtDCdfB3dhe?e=b8f90417f9&c2id=150df94da93954b2128cfda2414939d1)
---
**_Elegimos_ ran by House Majority PAC**
[ ](https://us.list-manage.com/R6PQbnfoOM7?e=b8f90417f9&c2id=150df94da93954b2128cfda2414939d1)
---
**Mailer ran by Unidos Action Fund **
| **CA-48: Marni Von Wilpert**
Our Spanish-language ads for House Majority PAC contrasted Marni’s career holding price-gouging corporations accountable with Jim Desmond’s record.
---
| [ ](https://us.list-manage.com/KBCYK5ItfHu?e=b8f90417f9&c2id=150df94da93954b2128cfda2414939d1)
---
**_Corrupto_ ran by House Majority PAC**

In solidarity,
Solidarity Strategies

## **New Leaders, Same Blind Spot: Why Republicans Haven 't Heart the Voters**
This week on Capitol Hill, House and Senate Republicans held their leadership elections to chart the path forward for the next Congress.
In the Senate, Republicans opted for complete continuity, reelecting their entire slate from last cycle - with Sen. John Thune remaining at the helm as he transitions into the role of Minority Leader. Over in the House, lawmakers shook things up by electing Ohio Rep. Jim Jordan over current Majority Leader Steve Scalise in a 106-73 secret ballot.

Both leaders immediately laid out how they plan to operate in the minority and go on offense against the incoming Democratic majorities. Fighting back against Democratic overreach and oversight battles is necessary - especially when the pressure mounts.
**But there is a massive piece missing from the equation: a real vision for the future.**
Voters sent an unmistakable message at the ballot box last week. They told us that daily life has become too expensive - from housing and energy bills to groceries and healthcare. Yet, when you ask people in Washington what Republicans are focused on right now, the answer you keep hearing is "permitting reform."
While the bill is important ask any American outside of a D.C. lobbyist what "permitting reform" actually means for their kitchen table, and they won't have a clue. The policy has to connect to the person -- if they don't have a clue what it means or how it will effect their life you have a problem.
With roughly 50 days left before the new Congress is sworn in on January 3, 2027, we are still failing to present tangible economic alternatives - and explaining how those policies actually improve people's lives.

John Thune remaining at the helm as he transitions into the role of Minority Leader. Over in the House, lawmakers shook things up by electing Ohio Rep. Jim Jordan over current Majority Leader Steve Scalise in a 106-73 secret ballot. Both leaders immediately laid out how they plan to operate in the minority and go on offense against the incoming Democratic majorities. name: Carrie Anne
subject: After the election: What now for Forward?
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Forward Party and not authorized by any candidate or candidate's committee
body:
Join our National Volunteer Call next Tues for updates on how election night went.

| | [ ](https://home.forwardparty.com/r?u=JgyyvCfQwldlSeD7KJl_Ih7269o_4hwqOhPs1_PHvgI&e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=forward_friends_nov_26&n=1)
---
| Hello Forward Friends- I don't know about you, but to me election night is very special, it reminds me of New Year's. On both nights you stay up late excitedly, and the morning brings new beginnings. This year America made history electing minority women. Unfortunately, though the pendulum of power just swung to the other side, with no change to the systems that got us here in the first place. Thus, our work continues! We had **38** Forward endorsed candidates win, with 3 of those being Independents elected to their state legislatures. Our federal level candidates pulled historic vote totals. If you like to hear more about our wins and what we accomplished this cycle, join our _National Volunteer Call_ this **Tues Nov 17th at 7:30pm ET** for an election recap. | [](https://home.forwardparty.com/national_volunteer_call_20261013_20261110?e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=forward_friends_nov_26&n=2 "RSVP FOR THE CALL") [RSVP FOR THE CALL](https://home.forwardparty.com/national_volunteer_call_20261013_20261110?e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=forward_friends_nov_26&n=2)
---
**_Text Banking Stats_**
Thanks to about 50 amazing volunteers, we were able to send out over **360,000** texts in support of **26** candidates. That's 100,000 more texts than we sent out in 2024! Special appreciation to our top 5 texters, **Wylene Small** with 82,126, **Ashley Rivera** with 75,860, **Jeanne Sole** with 60,744, **Kris Sun** with 41,325, and **Julie Brustman** with 35,763 texts sent. You guys are amazing! ** __**
**_Volunteer Spotlight_**
We had so many people who stepped up this election season. One story in particular was really moving. Our volunteer of the month, **Juli Servatius** **from MN** , was a total rockstar, and traveled to knock on doors with us in both South Carolina and South Dakota! While in SC she met **Kayla Sullivan** , our other volunteer of the month, who was a campaign manager for some local races there. Juli introduced Kayla to a Forward candidate needing help in MN, and Kayla jumped right in. It's so inspiring to see our supporters connecting across states to make a difference! Thank you, Juli and Kayla, for your dedication to this movement.
**Tues Nov 17th @ 7:30 pm ET** \- [National Volunteer Call](https://home.forwardparty.com/national_volunteer_call_20261013_20261110?e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=forward_friends_nov_26&n=3)
* Election recap edition! Join us for an overview of the party and how to use our website for volunteer resources. In this edition we will also talk about how our candidates did this election.

**Wed Dec 2nd @ 6:30pm ET** \- [Welcome Team Training](https://home.forwardparty.com/welcome_team_intro_call_20261012_20261202?e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=forward_friends_nov_26&n=4)
* Learn how to call other Forward supporters in your state and welcome them to the party! Script and template provided.

**Wed Dec 9nd @ 6:30pm ET** \- [Run for Office Webinar](https://home.forwardparty.com/run_for_office_dec_26?e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=forward_friends_nov_26&n=5)
* Are you ready to get in on the action? Learn how to get started and apply for the Forward endorsement at our webinar!

I had amazing time this election season. It was incredible to meet so many of you in person. The election may be over, but the party building never stops. Thank you so much to those of you who got involved this year- and if this wasn't your year to play a part, I look forward to plugging you in next year.
With gratitude,
Carrie Anne

name: Wally King, American Veterans Center
subject: I was a POW for two weeks
body:
My commander was right. Just not the way either of us meant.

| | | |
---
Friends,
---
On April 18, 1945, I walked up to my squadron commander and said, "This is my 75th mission. Don't you think it's time to quit?"He said, "Yeah. This is going to be your last mission."He was right. _Just not the way either of us meant._ My name is Wally King. I just turned 103. During World War II, I flew P-47 Thunderbolts over France and Germany with the 513th Fighter Squadron.
---
[](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyUkb-OnDAQh5_GdIcY22uWwkWU1Uop7tqU1mQYWOuwTWwDrx9xu12q60bz5_v00_x-d-_oFx_nDwxsafcuF-cPLLimY0q5Hulg_ixOdtK8AbyBckjV7-w0NqOl0SjZsIV-0JehA31tHpZJ0pWGq1Rm0BdSJDVPEoz8Y65mGvrG2xMHAAp6uKihnRSCZsCuJ2DsQehuW0esXFpKsXDe8XT6GNNZpdhSCs1iH7WuRagfQt6FvBemLXOLgbMnjDtXzhgLcayc25RnIe_zxqW64ufI-ZnKIf0V6l7SlokdpZGFuv389QFG6g6ENFsNLvDotyDUjQP65dV8ngh1e2AesXx-kZ4jwrCin6NQN9zJ_W997VXOJ7XJdlwPvyy-mF7obj4tXxnrt5-yW_kvAAD__9vxnm8)
---
I grew up in rural Ohio. I went to all 12 grades in the same school building, and my graduating class had 32 students. All 16 of the boys served in the war.I'd wanted to fly since I was a kid building model airplanes. The P-47 was a tough, honest airplane. It could take a beating and bring you home.The mission I remember most came just before Christmas 1944, during the Battle of the Bulge.Our job was to knock out the German guns around Bastogne before the supply planes came in. Everything was buried in snow.When the parachutes dropped, men who had been dug in under all that white came up out of the ground and started dragging those supplies into town.**Friends, I'll never forget that sight.** _Then came April 18._ On the way home, my wingman spotted a gun on a railroad car, and we went down for a look. Flak hit my engine. Fire came over the windshield.I bailed out over German territory with civilians shooting at me on the way down.Friends, I was beaten, burned and terrified. I'd never given God much thought before that day, but right then, a peace came over me like nothing I'd ever felt. It stayed with me the whole two weeks I was a prisoner.**And it was a German doctor who got me home.** He was caring for badly wounded Americans in a house near the Russian front. When the war was all but over, he rode with us in two ambulances to the American lines, driving after midnight with no lights.I've often wondered how many of those boys would have lived without him.
---
[](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyUkb-OnDAQh5_GdIcY22uWwkWU1Uop7tqU1mQYWOuwTWwDrx9xu12q60bz5_v00_x-d-_oFx_nDwxsafcuF-cPLLimY0q5Hulg_ixOdtK8AbyBckjV7-w0NqOl0SjZsIV-0JehA31tHpZJ0pWGq1Rm0BdSJDVPEoz8Y65mGvrG2xMHAAp6uKihnRSCZsCuJ2DsQehuW0esXFpKsXDe8XT6GNNZpdhSCs1iH7WuRagfQt6FvBemLXOLgbMnjDtXzhgLcayc25RnIe_zxqW64ufI-ZnKIf0V6l7SlokdpZGFuv389QFG6g6ENFsNLvDotyDUjQP65dV8ngh1e2AesXx-kZ4jwrCin6NQN9zJ_W997VXOJ7XJdlwPvyy-mF7obj4tXxnrt5-yW_kvAAD__9vxnm8)
---
_Above: I met with the boys of the 117_ _th_ _Air Refueling Wing of the Alabama National Guard before flying to Normandy, France in June 2025 for the 81_ _st_ _anniversary of D-Day. _
---
For years now, I've talked to students about the war.**What troubles me, Friends, is how little young Americans know about World War II.** When students ask me for advice, I tell them: _put down your cell phones and love one another._ But I can't get to every classroom, Friends.**That's why I'm writing to you on behalf of the American Veterans Center. They make sure the next generation hears the truth from the people who lived it.** AVC is a nonprofit educational organization dedicated to preserving and promoting the legacy of America's veterans and active-duty service members, from World War II through today. Its work includes:
---
* **The National Memorial Day Parade** in Washington, D.C., the nation's largest Memorial Day event
* **The Annual Veterans Conference** every Veterans Day weekend, where veterans of every generation share their stories with hundreds of cadets and midshipmen
* **AMERICAN VALOR: A Salute to Our Heroes,** a two-time Emmy-winning special broadcast nationwide

clean_body: My commander was right. Just not the way either of us meant. | | | | Friends, On April 18, 1945, I walked up to my squadron commander and said, "This is my 75th mission. Don't you think it's time to quit?"He said, "Yeah. This is going to be your last mission."He was right. Just not the way either of us meant. My name is Wally King. I just turned 103. During World War II, I flew P-47 Thunderbolts over France and Germany with the 513th Fighter Squadron. I grew up in rural Ohio. I went to all 12 grades in the same school building, and my graduating class had 32 students. All 16 of the boys served in the war.I'd wanted to fly since I was a kid building model airplanes. The P-47 was a tough, honest airplane. It could take a beating and bring you home.The mission I remember most came just before Christmas 1944, during the Battle of the Bulge.Our job was to knock out the German guns around Bastogne before the supply planes came in. Everything was buried in snow.When the parachutes dropped, men who had been dug in under all that white came up out of the ground and started dragging those supplies into town.Friends, I'll never forget that sight. Then came April 18. On the way home, my wingman spotted a gun on a railroad car, and we went down for a look. Flak hit my engine. Fire came over the windshield.I bailed out over German territory with civilians shooting at me on the way down.Friends, I was beaten, burned and terrified. I'd never given God much thought before that day, but right then, a peace came over me like nothing I'd ever felt. It stayed with me the whole two weeks I was a prisoner.And it was a German doctor who got me home. He was caring for badly wounded Americans in a house near the Russian front. When the war was all but over, he rode with us in two ambulances to the American lines, driving after midnight with no lights.I've often wondered how many of those boys would have lived without him. Above: I met with the boys of the 117 th Air Refueling Wing of the Alabama National Guard before flying to Normandy, France in June 2025 for the 81 st anniversary of D-Day. For years now, I've talked to students about the war.What troubles me, Friends, is how little young Americans know about World War II. When students ask me for advice, I tell them: put down your cell phones and love one another. But I can't get to every classroom, Friends.That's why I'm writing to you on behalf of the American Veterans Center. They make sure the next generation hears the truth from the people who lived it. AVC is a nonprofit educational organization dedicated to preserving and promoting the legacy of America's veterans and active-duty service members, from World War II through today. Derek, I want you
to hear me on this:

Once our Democratic trifecta is sworn into office in January, we’re not
going to waste a second.

We’re going to more than double Pennsylvania’s minimum wage.

We’re going to codify abortion rights into our state Constitution.

We’re going to fund mass transit.

We’re going to build more housing.

These are the commonsense things that Pennsylvanians want done. Voters
made that crystal clear exactly ten days ago.

And with a Democratic trifecta, we’ll deliver on every single one of them.
You have my word on that.

Derek, I’ve always
believed in reaching across the aisle to get things done. I’ve done it for
nearly four years at this point — serving as one of just a handful of
governors working with a divided legislature.

But Republicans learned something this year: If you’re going to screw over
Pennsylvania families — by cutting SNAP benefits, gutting healthcare, or
wrecking every opportunity to raise the minimum wage here in PA — we’re
going to hold you accountable at the ballot box.

Folks here in Pennsylvania voted for a different future. A better future.

Peter,

This week, I joined the rest of the incoming class of the 120th Congress for New Member Orientation, and I want you to be among the first to hear how it went.

As a teacher, the best way I can describe it is the first day of school before classes actually begin. We spent the week getting to know the colleagues we’ll be serving alongside, both new and longtime members of the House, and getting an early look at the agenda that will be waiting for us when the new Congress begins.
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/143405770/660104097/902181018?refcode=em-11.13.26-all&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjIvMS8xMTc1MjUiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiMGU1NWQzZGYtODdkZi1mMTExLTkxZjAtMDAwZDNhMThlMjQ0IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=AjIiwnOy4JX-I8MkuD5sN8C9w1-cIh3kbvnuUOkbvDo=)
I had a great time meeting so many new people, but I went into every meeting and every conversation with one question in mind: how can I deliver for the families of the Central Valley? That will be my focus from day one.

Between now and swearing-in, I’ll keep you updated on how we’re preparing to hit the ground running. **If you have questions, concerns, or something you want me to know about what matters most to you, just hit reply to this email, because I want to hear from you.**

Before I go, there’s one more thing I want to ask of you. Not every Democrat elected this month has had their race called yet, and some outgoing Republicans are clinging to power by forcing recounts in races they lost.

**One of them is my fellow educator Jake Johnson in Minnesota, who is leading by just over 300 votes in a district Trump won by 12 points. A recount is expensive, and Jake needs the resources to make sure every legal ballot is counted and this seat doesn’t slip away.**

Thank you for everything. I’ll be in touch soon.

Randy

| Even Tech CEOs Are Not Immune to Romance Scams
---
For decades, Nvidia has been one of the world's largest producers of graphics processing units (GPUs). The increased demand for GPUs for use in AI data centers over the last few years has made Nvidia very profitable and has also made it a major target for espionage, as the company's CEO, Jensen Huang, has admitted to an affair with a woman, Alice Huang (no relation), who is [suspected of being a spy](https://click.iphonelife.com/ga/click/2-17209631-109-17167-260921-8907314-b54208a0e0-dh43ff9811) for the Chinese Ministry of State Security.Ms. Huang is [reportedly an executive at Megaspeed](https://click.iphonelife.com/ga/click/2-17209631-109-17167-260921-8907316-3691252d61-dh43ff9811), a data center firm based out of Singapore. It is believed that through her relationship with Jensen Huang, she was able to purchase hundreds of thousands of Nvidia chips and GPUs for her company, some of which went to data centers based in China. China is aiming to become the leader in AI technology, and Ms. Huang's ability to acquire chips otherwise restricted from being sold in the country gave it the edge it needed to achieve that goal.Jensen Huang [has resigned](https://click.iphonelife.com/ga/click/2-17209631-109-17167-260921-8907317-93d1610bda-dh43ff9811), and Congress has requested a closed-door briefing with him to discuss his affair, while the FBI is currently investigating the matter. The [Chinese government has denied any involvement](https://click.iphonelife.com/ga/click/2-17209631-109-17167-260921-8907319-31cd4e0cdc-dh43ff9811) with Alice Huang.**The Bottom Line** : When you boil this situation down to its core, it's really just an extremely sophisticated version of the romance scam. A romance scam involves someone building a relationship with you, gaining your trust, and eventually asking for help, usually in the form of money for medical bills or travel expenses so that they can come see you. Romance scams can go on for months (or, in the case of Mr. Huang, years) while the scammer builds trust with you, making you believe they are your friend or that they've fallen in love with you.Everyone is susceptible to this type of scam, even billionaire tech CEOs. And you don't have to be a billionaire CEO to be targeted. Romance scammers will go after retirees or whoever they think is the most vulnerable, whether they're wealthy or not.

## Still Using iOS 18? Time to Update
Last month, we reported on a new spyware infection technique, which [The Citizen Lab dubbed AdFection](https://click.iphonelife.com/ga/click/2-17209631-109-17167-260921-8907320-91cfff951d-dh43ff9811). At the time, we believed the primary targets of AdFection were specific individuals, like politicians, journalists, and activists. Now, mobile security platform iVerify is warning that AdFection is under active exploitation by hackers who are using it to infect iPhones with DarkSword, an iOS-based infostealer malware that is designed to steal passwords, photos, messages, or anything else that might seem valuable. Anyone with iOS devices still on iOS 18.4 through 18.7 is vulnerable. AdFection requires no interaction from the user; all it takes is being served one malicious ad, whether it's in your favorite social media app or while browsing the web. Read the full report at [iVerify](https://click.iphonelife.com/ga/click/2-17209631-109-17167-260921-8907321-4d9470e19c-dh43ff9811).**The Bottom Line** : DarkSword only affects iPhones running iOS 18.4 to 18.7, so as long as you're running the latest software, you should be safe. If your iPhone cannot update beyond iOS 18, it may be time to upgrade.
## FBI Outsourcing Investigative Work to AI
This week, FBI director Kash Patel did a deep dive into how the bureau is using AI to boost efficiency and reduce staff workload. According to Patel, the FBI is using AI to automate transcription and translation work. In one example, the agency used AI to transcribe hundreds of hours of audio from a wiretap in order to accelerate the rescue of a human trafficking victim. Head over to [NextGov](https://click.iphonelife.com/ga/click/2-17209631-109-17167-260921-8907322-0debf55b25-dh43ff9811) for Patel's full statement.**The Bottom Line** : At first glance, it almost sounds like this is a positive use for AI. It's reducing the FBI's workload and allowing it to move through investigations more quickly. However, we remain skeptical of outsourcing forensic investigative decisions to AI. AI cannot be held responsible for its decisions or its mistakes, and going fast is not the same as being right. Translation software can be a powerful tool, but when the outcome matters, remember to always manually check the results.

## Sleep-Tracking Headbands Might Be Using Your Data for AI
Electroencephalogram (EEG) headbands are popular for tracking sleep and learning from your sleep patterns. These headbands record your brain waves and transform that activity into readable data. As it turns out, many manufacturers (such as Interaxon, the parent company of the popular Muse headband) are using the collected data to train AI. These companies don't make it explicitly clear to the user how their data is being used. Muse's privacy policy was only updated recently to clarify that data from electrical brain activity is being used for AI training. Check out the full story at [Tom's Hardware](https://click.iphonelife.com/ga/click/2-17209631-109-17167-260921-8907324-9de7fdfd6f-dh43ff9811).**The Bottom Line** : HIPAA privacy rules only apply to health information you share with your healthcare provider, not information you share with a private company like Muse. Legally, there's nothing stopping these headband companies from collecting and using this data however they please, as long as it's disclosed in their privacy policies. If tracking your sleep is important to you, we recommend using an Apple Watch for privacy. It won't scan your brainwaves like an EEG headband, but it still has its uses.
## UK Government Sites Left Vulnerable
Security researcher Chris Nesbitt-Smith has identified a number of vulnerabilities in the code of multiple UK government websites. He found the vulnerabilities using two Claude AI models. For transparency purposes, the UK government publicly posts the source code of its websites online for anyone to access. This is not an abnormal process; for example, Apple makes the source code of Private Cloud Compute publicly available so that independent researchers can verify its privacy and security. However, the side effect of making that data public means vulnerabilities can be found, both by researchers and by cybercriminals using AI. Read more at [Wired](https://click.iphonelife.com/ga/click/2-17209631-109-17167-260921-8907325-af32f6a624-dh43ff9811).**The Bottom Line** : AI is a double-edged sword for the cybersecurity sector. It can be used by researchers to expose bugs and vulnerabilities, but it can also be used by bad actors for the same purpose. With cybersecurity firms stretched thin, it's difficult to patch all of these newfound vulnerabilities before hackers can exploit them.

## Mozilla VPN Offering Unlimited Data for Free Until New Year
Earlier this year, Mozilla added a free VPN built into its Firefox web browser. Normally, it includes 50 GB of data that can be used for free, after which you'll need to pay a subscription fee to continue using it. However, starting now through January 31, 2027, Mozilla VPN is getting unlimited data. That means you can change your location and hide your web traffic on public Wi-Fi as much as you want, free of charge, until the New Year. [Mozilla's blog post](https://click.iphonelife.com/ga/click/2-17209631-109-17167-260921-8907326-d0f002440d-dh43ff9811) has more details.The Bottom Line: It's important to keep in mind that Mozilla's free browser VPN does not make you anonymous online, and it only affects your web traffic within Firefox. If you need truly private internet access and need your VPN to work outside of Firefox, we recommend a standalone VPN, like NordVPN or Mullvad.
## How Scammers Use Social Media to Tailor Scams to You
Scammers are continuing to find new ways to use AI to their advantage. One such method is to use your social media. By plugging in publicly available social media data, scammers can send out phishing texts or emails custom-tailored to your personal details. In the example provided by [Fox News](https://click.iphonelife.com/ga/click/2-17209631-109-17167-260921-8907327-d52798d3c0-dh43ff9811), a scammer-controlled AI could find photos you posted of a recent vacation and generate an email appearing to be from the hotel you stayed at, ensuring you're more likely to open any links in the email.The Bottom Line: Identifying suspicious emails can be difficult, especially when they're carefully designed to look legitimate. Always be on your guard when it comes to emails, and look for [signs of phishing](https://click.iphonelife.com/ga/click/2-17209631-109-17167-260921-8907328-289ff5fbf2-dh43ff9811).

## EU Aims to Curtail Infinite Doomscrolling & Other Manipulative Design Techniques
The EU is proposing a new law, called the Digital Fairness Act, to combat apps and websites with anticonsumer practices, like promoting addictive behaviors or the unnecessary difficulties of canceling subscriptions. The Digital Fairness Act is a part of a larger initiative to strengthen EU consumer laws. However, it's nothing more than an outline of what lawmakers hope to achieve; no law has been passed at the moment. Find out more and read the full text of the Digital Fairness Act at the [European Commission](https://click.iphonelife.com/ga/click/2-17209631-109-17167-260921-8907329-541bba62d7-dh43ff9811).**The Bottom Line** : While the Digital Fairness Act is only a proposal at this time, it's certainly a step in the right direction. We hope that it can lead to something fruitful that will ultimately improve the internet for everyone.

## Hackers Flush Out Customer Data from TP Company
Who Gives a Crap is the name of a toilet paper brand that supplies eco-friendly toilet paper made from recycled materials. The company has been hit by a data breach through a third-party marketing provider, exposing customer names, addresses, emails, and phone numbers. Customers from the US, UK, and Australia have all been affected. Unfortunately, Who Gives a Crap will need more than toilet paper to clean up the mess it has found itself in. It has cut all ties with the marketing company where the breach originated. Read the full story in [The Register](https://click.iphonelife.com/ga/click/2-17209631-109-17167-260921-8907331-bd70a74dda-dh43ff9811).**The Bottom Line** : Despite the company's name, Who Gives a Crap appears to care very much about its customers and is working to amend the damage done by this breach. If you've ever purchased from Who Gives a Crap, your data might be exposed. As always, when it comes to data breaches, we recommend freezing your credit, which can be done online at the three major credit bureaus.

---|---|---
Rene Cobos Merchan on set of an international media set. Photo provided to Drop Site by Rene Cobos Merchan's family.
At half past midnight on August 23, six masked assailants stepped out of two pickup trucks onto the makeshift streets of Tres Postes, Ecuador, dressed in a mix of military uniforms and police vests, their guns locked and loaded. They had come to kill Rene Manuel Cobos Merchan, a beloved local journalist and freelance producer.
The uniformed _sicarios_ approached Cobos's home, a small single-story residence adjoined to his girlfriend's nephew's home. The two houses sit with almost identical white doors beneath a single corrugated tin roof. In what family members believe was a mistake, the gunmen burst through the nephew's door, barking "Where's the _se ñor_ from the yellow taxi?" They shot the young man, instantly killing him. The assailants then forced their way into Cobos's home, closing in on him at gunpoint.
Cobos, known for driving a yellow taxi cab as his personal car, had built a resume guiding some of the most recognized names in journalism--Al Jazeera, PBS, Channel 4--through the armed conflict engulfing his, and so many Ecuadorians', working-class neighborhoods. He brokered exclusive interviews with underground figures, scouting locations, arranging transportation, getting reporters in and out of the field, and supplying the kind of sociopolitical context one only really gains from growing up somewhere.
This critical role is often referred to as a "fixer," a term commonly used to describe local media workers--often in the global south--who help journalists from other countries--often in the global north--report and produce stories for media outlets in their countries. Many reject the title, arguing it undersells the expertise and labor involved.
Cobos had most recently worked on a widely viewed BBC documentary exposing Ecuador's brutal drug war and corrupt cops, according to five sources interviewed by Drop Site, drawing a slew of death threats against him. In fact, both Cobos's and his nephew's homes appear in the BBC film, "Police Fight Gangs, Guns And Corruption In Ecuador's War On Drugs," Cobos's eldest daughter told Drop Site. A longtime colleague of Cobos's, who spoke to Drop Site on the condition of anonymity for fear of his life, said the BBC used Cobos's bedroom to film interviews with gang members--the very room he was later killed in.
In the days leading up to his assassination, Cobos frantically confided in a family friend and three colleagues that he was receiving death threats. He believed the threats were retaliation for his role in the BBC documentary, for which he had coordinated key sources, securing the British broadcaster exclusive access to both police operations and the black market.
"The police are not happy" with the documentary, Cobos anxiously told Guilermo Galdos, a friend and Channel 4 journalist, in one of their last conversations. Galdos recalled Cobos saying that police wanted comments about narco infiltration of law enforcement, made in an on-the-record interview by Captain Jean Carlos Bustamante, removed.
When Drop Site asked the BBC and its reporter for comment on Cobos's death and its possible link to the documentary, which was filmed in his home, the BBC said that Cobos did not work for the network. Asked whether he had been involved in any way with the production, the BBC said Cobos was not hired by them. It is not unusual for fixers to be hired informally on a cash only and contract basis and not directly by a network. Drop Site confirmed that photos of his room and the home's exterior match the documentary. Drop Site provided the BBC with screenshots of the documentary where family members say the homes appear, along with follow-up questions, and the BBC did not reply.
When the National Police's homicide and forensic units arrived on scene, they recovered 30 spent shell casings of 20 9mm and ten 5.56mm bullets. A police officer, who spoke to Drop Site on the condition of anonymity, confirmed these are the standard models used by Ecuadorian police.
The National Police later confirmed to [Fundamedios](https://substack.com/redirect/11b0f2ff-4670-46c7-8a62-ed96ce31b203?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that he had received death threats. Drop Site requested an official police report and statements from the National Police Directorate, including about the death threats Cobos had received, and contacted five law-enforcement officers for comment. The Directorate referred questions to the Attorney General's office, which did not respond.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/3af9e7a3-c964-4b23-9b89-d59e2a3497aa?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
A screenshot of the BBC film, annotated by a family member to show Cobos's and the nephew's doors.
Cobos, a father of six and "tio" to the neighborhood kids, grew up along the Ecuadorian coast--[where six of the world's most dangerous cities now sit](https://substack.com/redirect/83a825a0-441e-4689-ac61-1312321876c9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)--and took immense pride in producing stories from the region. His eldest daughter told Drop Site that he would send her photos each time he was on set. He had a habit of hosting family watch parties, squeezing all his loved ones around the TV in their tiny living room, to watch the latest documentary he'd worked on. Half-chuckling, half holding-back tears, a separate family member fondly recalled how he would pause the documentary at each scene or interview he'd help set up, just to make sure all eyes were on the screen.
In one scene of the BBC documentary, a man affiliated with a drug-trafficking group sits atop Rene's bed and boasts that he has four police officers on his payroll. In another scene during a counternarcotics operation, Bustamante, the police captain, tells the cameras, "We have many, many bad people inside the [police] unit, inside the state, inside politics. We have many guys that are corrupted. They are in the pay of the gangs."
Under the right-wing regime of President Daniel Noboa--the Miami-born, Harvard-educated heir to a billion-dollar banana conglomerate with its own history of drug-trafficking allegations--Ecuador has become the [most violent country](https://substack.com/redirect/0ee82192-27d8-4b26-9647-e26c819820fb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in the Western Hemisphere. A staggering 70% percent of the world's cocaine moves through Ecuador's ports en route to Europe and the United States, the world's largest consumer. Critics nicknamed the embattled president "Narco Noboa" after local authorities discovered 26 million euros' worth of cocaine stashed in cargo boxes aboard the boats of his family's banana export business--a business of which Noboa is the majority shareholder, the Pandora Papers revealed. Nevertheless, Noboa claims he is on a crusade to crush the cartels, invoking 23 martial law decrees, authorizing U.S. ground strikes, and racking up human rights violations.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/78a9af97-c5ba-4d77-ab7e-21ee6a5e9a5b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
A sign from nationwide protests against Noboa says, "Reject the narco-dictator government." Photo by Maria Jativa @Mariastyle13/Medio Chiro Digital.
Caught between state crackdowns on free speech and cartel kill orders, the press and whistleblowers have absorbed some of the worst consequences of the armed conflict. Between 2025 and 2026 alone, Ecuador dropped 31 rankings on the World Press Freedom index. Speaking to an Ecuadorian TV network, Ecuavisa, the Director for the Americas Division at Human Rights Watch, Juanita Goebertus said, "The Noboa government appears to be more effective at attacking civil society organizations and opposition parties than it is at attacking organized crime."
Many media workers in Ecuador fear that they will meet the same harrowing fate that Cobos did. More than 800 attacks on the press have been recorded across the country since 2022. The state was the single largest culprit of intimidation against journalists this year; responsible for 46 of the 100 assaults and threats [recorded between January and June by Fundamedios](https://substack.com/redirect/6bb3c6e8-dea1-4b3c-8ee1-b914abf2d1e2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). By comparison, organized crime groups accounted for five of the attacks on the press this year, according to the outfit.
On Sunday, November 8, investigative journalist Tomas Beltran was shot and killed in his garage. His murder follows months of death threats, which began after he filed a complaint accusing Ledy Muñoz, his local mayor and a member of Noboa's party, of illicit enrichment. In response to the threats, Beltran had been placed under a protection program by the Attorney General's office.
In June, Monika Silva Koniuszek, a whistleblower who had delivered evidence of Noboa's illicit business activities to the U.S. embassy in Quito, was found dead in her home. The post-mortem examination discovered blows to her head. Friends and family say that her murder was intended to silence her investigation of Noboa. One of her associates, the journalist Gabriela Pachana, was subsequently [sentenced to 30 days in jail](https://substack.com/redirect/8a34058b-1367-42c9-9356-db62c57395a8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) for suggesting as much in a post on X.
That same month, over 20 human rights organizations issued [a joint statement](https://substack.com/redirect/67ef1dda-3b5c-4776-a560-8a21928ee042?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) warning that the numerous threats and assaults on the press "reflect an alarming trend." "The fight against corruption and the demand for accountability have become high-risk activities in Ecuador," they wrote, adding that, under the new martial law regime, "lack of transparency and opacity are becoming consolidated as State policy."
Through recent martial-law decrees, the government has granted itself the authority to wiretap communications without probable cause or warrants, further undermining journalists' ability to communicate safely and securely with whistleblowers and other sensitive sources.
Newsrooms have also come under threat. In September of 2025, [a local television station](https://substack.com/redirect/c488e642-29ca-40a8-8bef-35ae57656f1f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) was suspended after Ecuadorian intelligence agencies deemed it a threat to national security for broadcasting footage of protests and labor strikes by Indigenous activists, which Noboa branded "terrorism."
In April, Bloomberg News highlighted the erosion of civil liberties and press freedom under the Noboa administration after several board members of two Ecuadorian news outlets faced criminal charges amid their refusal to sell 40% of their shares to the government. One of the outlets, Diario Expreso, [was forced to shut down its 53-year print edition](https://substack.com/redirect/af505ae8-377d-4def-ac04-1bbe239a1eb7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) after 70% of advertisers withdrew under pressure from the state.
Another prominent Ecuadorian publication, GK, indefinitely suspended all operations on October 29 and warned that, "The context in Ecuador is not favorable for independent journalism. We have sadly witnessed the closure of other media outlets due to political pressure, and the persecution of reporters simply for doing their job and holding those in power accountable."
The Director-General of UNESCO condemned Cobos's death, demanding an investigation and accountability. "Impunity for such crimes is unacceptable and must not be tolerated," the Director-General said.
Cobos himself was deeply critical of the economy and risks around being a fixer, Galdos told Drop Site. "This is the fifth contact of mine that has been killed," Galdos said. "The fifth person I've worked with who opened a window for me to get to know the underworld and who today is no longer with us because that's how dangerous the issue is." Galdos said that Cobos's face carried a faded scar because hitmen "had already tried to kill him years ago."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/df01f44c-b3da-4c6e-b53f-00a9df2d4594?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Rene Manuel Cobos Merchan (second from the right) on set with Al Jazeera Fault Lines.
Hailing from Duran, [ranked the world's most dangerous city in the world in 2023](https://substack.com/redirect/e63436a6-30e6-4750-a460-35a78d208c50?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), where daily life is interspersed with crime scenes and shoot outs, Cobos had documented both the bloodshed and corruption of the drug war.
And he was attentive to the effects of violence in his community. Friends, fellow journalists, and family recalled how he helped mothers of gun-violence victims relocate to safety, including one woman who lost her four sons and husband to shootings last year, who says Cobos helped pay her month-to-month rent. He would tell and retell the same stories--which always carried a lesson--to the neighborhood kids no matter how many times they had heard them.
Josh Rushing and Jeremy Young, both Emmy-winning journalists with Al Jazeera, recounted how Cobos may have saved their lives while they were filming in Ecuador in 2023. After a smuggler they had arranged to interview called and threatened them, Cobos urged them to take the threats seriously and leave Salinas. With roads about to close for the elections, he drove to their hotel at 10 p.m., got them out, and brought them safely to Guayaquil. "He put himself in danger to do it," Rushing said.
Reeling from the loss, his family is terrified that pressing the authorities on his death could make them targets too. "I know it shouldn't just be left like this, but it's also so scary. To avoid problems, it's better not to ask or investigate anything ourselves," his eldest daughter told Drop Site.
For families like Cobos's, answers may never come. Fewer than 10% of homicide cases in the region are solved. But even if the case is buried, his legacy will not be. "When everyone around there found out that Rene had died, the whole neighborhood, everyone there, was devastated, because he had helped a lot of people," a loved one said.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/8fc1363d-b8b7-46ce-933d-45f5b763b082?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
