When the National Police's homicide and forensic units arrived on scene, they recovered 30 spent shell casings of 20 9mm and ten 5.56mm bullets. A police officer, who spoke to Drop Site on the condition of anonymity, confirmed these are the standard models used by Ecuadorian police. The National Police later confirmed to that he had received death threats. Drop Site requested an official police report and statements from the National Police Directorate, including about the death threats Cobos had received, and contacted five law-enforcement officers for comment. The Directorate referred questions to the Attorney General's office, which did not respond. | | ---|---|--- A screenshot of the BBC film, annotated by a family member to show Cobos's and the nephew's doors. Cobos, a father of six and "tio" to the neighborhood kids, grew up along the Ecuadorian coast-- took immense pride in producing stories from the region. His eldest daughter told Drop Site that he would send her photos each time he was on set. He had a habit of hosting family watch parties, squeezing all his loved ones around the TV in their tiny living room, to watch the latest documentary he'd worked on. Half-chuckling, half holding-back tears, a separate family member fondly recalled how he would pause the documentary at each scene or interview he'd help set up, just to make sure all eyes were on the screen. In one scene of the BBC documentary, a man affiliated with a drug-trafficking group sits atop Rene's bed and boasts that he has four police officers on his payroll. In another scene during a counternarcotics operation, Bustamante, the police captain, tells the cameras, "We have many, many bad people inside the [police] unit, inside the state, inside politics. We have many guys that are corrupted. They are in the pay of the gangs." Under the right-wing regime of President Daniel Noboa--the Miami-born, Harvard-educated heir to a billion-dollar banana conglomerate with its own history of drug-trafficking allegations--Ecuador has become the in the Western Hemisphere. A staggering 70% percent of the world's cocaine moves through Ecuador's ports en route to Europe and the United States, the world's largest consumer. Critics nicknamed the embattled president "Narco Noboa" after local authorities discovered 26 million euros' worth of cocaine stashed in cargo boxes aboard the boats of his family's banana export business--a business of which Noboa is the majority shareholder, the Pandora Papers revealed. Nevertheless, Noboa claims he is on a crusade to crush the cartels, invoking 23 martial law decrees, authorizing U.S. ground strikes, and racking up human rights violations. | | ---|---|--- A sign from nationwide protests against Noboa says, "Reject the narco-dictator government." Photo by Maria Jativa @Mariastyle13/Medio Chiro Digital. Caught between state crackdowns on free speech and cartel kill orders, the press and whistleblowers have absorbed some of the worst consequences of the armed conflict. Between 2025 and 2026 alone, Ecuador dropped 31 rankings on the World Press Freedom index. Speaking to an Ecuadorian TV network, Ecuavisa, the Director for the Americas Division at Human Rights Watch, Juanita Goebertus said, "The Noboa government appears to be more effective at attacking civil society organizations and opposition parties than it is at attacking organized crime." Many media workers in Ecuador fear that they will meet the same harrowing fate that Cobos did. More than 800 attacks on the press have been recorded across the country since 2022. The state was the single largest culprit of intimidation against journalists this year; responsible for 46 of the 100 assaults and threats . By comparison, organized crime groups accounted for five of the attacks on the press this year, according to the outfit. On Sunday, November 8, investigative journalist Tomas Beltran was shot and killed in his garage. His murder follows months of death threats, which began after he filed a complaint accusing Ledy Muñoz, his local mayor and a member of Noboa's party, of illicit enrichment. In response to the threats, Beltran had been placed under a protection program by the Attorney General's office. In June, Monika Silva Koniuszek, a whistleblower who had delivered evidence of Noboa's illicit business activities to the U.S. embassy in Quito, was found dead in her home. The post-mortem examination discovered blows to her head. Friends and family say that her murder was intended to silence her investigation of Noboa. One of her associates, the journalist Gabriela Pachana, was subsequently for suggesting as much in a post on X. That same month, over 20 human rights organizations issued warning that the numerous threats and assaults on the press "reflect an alarming trend." "The fight against corruption and the demand for accountability have become high-risk activities in Ecuador," they wrote, adding that, under the new martial law regime, "lack of transparency and opacity are becoming consolidated as State policy." Through recent martial-law decrees, the government has granted itself the authority to wiretap communications without probable cause or warrants, further undermining journalists' ability to communicate safely and securely with whistleblowers and other sensitive sources. Newsrooms have also come under threat. In September of 2025, was suspended after Ecuadorian intelligence agencies deemed it a threat to national security for broadcasting footage of protests and labor strikes by Indigenous activists, which Noboa branded "terrorism." In April, Bloomberg News highlighted the erosion of civil liberties and press freedom under the Noboa administration after several board members of two Ecuadorian news outlets faced criminal charges amid their refusal to sell 40% of their shares to the government. One of the outlets, Diario Expreso, after 70% of advertisers withdrew under pressure from the state. Another prominent Ecuadorian publication, GK, indefinitely suspended all operations on October 29 and warned that, "The context in Ecuador is not favorable for independent journalism. We have sadly witnessed the closure of other media outlets due to political pressure, and the persecution of reporters simply for doing their job and holding those in power accountable." The Director-General of UNESCO condemned Cobos's death, demanding an investigation and accountability. "Impunity for such crimes is unacceptable and must not be tolerated," the Director-General said. Cobos himself was deeply critical of the economy and risks around being a fixer, Galdos told Drop Site. "This is the fifth contact of mine that has been killed," Galdos said. "The fifth person I've worked with who opened a window for me to get to know the underworld and who today is no longer with us because that's how dangerous the issue is." Galdos said that Cobos's face carried a faded scar because hitmen "had already tried to kill him years ago." | | ---|---|--- Rene Manuel Cobos Merchan (second from the right) on set with Al Jazeera Fault Lines. Hailing from Duran, , where daily life is interspersed with crime scenes and shoot outs, Cobos had documented both the bloodshed and corruption of the drug war. And he was attentive to the effects of violence in his community. Friends, fellow journalists, and family recalled how he helped mothers of gun-violence victims relocate to safety, including one woman who lost her four sons and husband to shootings last year, who says Cobos helped pay her month-to-month rent. He would tell and retell the same stories--which always carried a lesson--to the neighborhood kids no matter how many times they had heard them. Josh Rushing and Jeremy Young, both Emmy-winning journalists with Al Jazeera, recounted how Cobos may have saved their lives while they were filming in Ecuador in 2023. After a smuggler they had arranged to interview called and threatened them, Cobos urged them to take the threats seriously and leave Salinas. With roads about to close for the elections, he drove to their hotel at 10 p.m., got them out, and brought them safely to Guayaquil. "He put himself in danger to do it," Rushing said. Reeling from the loss, his family is terrified that pressing the authorities on his death could make them targets too. "I know it shouldn't just be left like this, but it's also so scary. To avoid problems, it's better not to ask or investigate anything ourselves," his eldest daughter told Drop Site. For families like Cobos's, answers may never come. Fewer than 10% of homicide cases in the region are solved. But even if the case is buried, his legacy will not be. "When everyone around there found out that Rene had died, the whole neighborhood, everyone there, was devastated, because he had helped a lot of people," a loved one said. | | ---|---|--- Cobos on the set of a media production. Friend,
Last week, voters across the nation sent a clear message: The American people are ready for change.
Donald Trump and his allies could see this coming. They knew that the country was outraged by their disastrous agenda.
That’s precisely _why_ they desperately tried to rig this election with partisan gerrymandering to stop voters from holding them accountable. That’s precisely _why_ they redrew congressional maps to dilute the voices of Black and brown voters – all to hold onto their own power.
Their plan spectacularly backfired.
On Election Day, you showed up. And their rigged maps and crooked lines all came crashing down.
**Now, it’s time to ban this partisan gerrymandering once and for all. If you’re ready to ensure fair maps and equal representation in every election going forward, I hope you’ll add your voice to mine today.**

subject: It started with January 6. It didn't end there.

A Special Message from our SponsorPlease note that views expressed in this message do not necessarily reflect those of Free Speech Daily and do not constitute an endorsement or recommendation by Free Speech Daily.
Shane Jenkins

https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABl7ImQiOjUwNjAsInQiOjc2NywicyI6MTJ9AAwAAAAABBuihhx5NCN4lSPsxmdPiWWFrB4Bz1S4rl8s9mgF4mwR70sDiuuJVvs9W4U1sEMOHK1oAmMRW2p6x3tnm3b-1GplZO5uJSbNGACK9WeH

Patriot,

Stand In The Gap Foundation was born out of January 6. For years, we stood beside those families. We paid for lawyers, covered rent, sat in courtrooms, and made sure nobody went through it alone.

What we learned in those years is why I'm writing to you today.

The lawfare that came down on January 6 families wasn't built for them, and it didn't stop with them.

So we widened the fight. Everything we built for those families now lives inside our Stand for Justice initiative, and Stand for Justice is now open to anyone the federal system has run over.

January 6 families aren't going anywhere. They're still with us. They're just no longer the only ones we can help.

Yesterday, I mailed the letter that opens this new chapter.

It went to the Office of the Pardon Attorney at the U.S. Department of Justice. It's about a man named Dr. Michael Rimlawi. His patients call him Dr. Mike.

Dr. Mike is a spine surgeon from Dallas. For twenty years, people came to him when they couldn't sit through a workday, couldn't pick up their kids, couldn't sleep through the night. He did the small-incision kind of spine surgery. Less cutting, less blood, and most patients home the same day or the next.

Then the federal government went after the hospital where he operated.

Forest Park Medical Center paid a marketing firm to advertise its surgeons, something hospitals all over this country do every day. Prosecutors called it a kickback. Dr. Mike wasn't charged with hurting a patient. He wasn't charged with billing for a surgery that never happened.

A jury convicted him in 2019. In 2021, a federal judge sentenced him to 90 months in prison, seven and a half years, and ordered him to pay $28,839,201.68 in restitution.

To insurance companies.

The Supreme Court refused to hear his case. Justice Gorsuch wrote that he would have heard it, because a judge, not a jury, set that $28.8 million.

Dr. Mike did his time. He's home now with his wife and their two young sons. But unless something changes, that debt follows him for twenty years after his release. And a pardon alone won't erase it. The pardon has to say so.

So our letter asks for two things: a full pardon, and that the pardon wipe out every dollar of restitution he hasn't paid.

Patriot, Dr. Mike was nowhere near the Capitol. But if you've followed what happened to January 6 families, you already know this story. A prosecution built to make an example. A sentence that ends on paper and keeps going in real life. Restitution that follows a man home and sits at his kitchen table.

Different courtroom. Same pattern.

That's why Dr. Mike is the first story we're telling from the new Stand for Justice. He won't be the last.

Shane Jenkins Patriot, Stand In The Gap Foundation was born out of January 6. For years, we stood beside those families. We paid for lawyers, covered rent, sat in courtrooms, and made sure nobody went through it alone. What we learned in those years is why I'm writing to you today. The lawfare that came down on January 6 families wasn't built for them, and it didn't stop with them. So we widened the fight. Everything we built for those families now lives inside our Stand for Justice initiative, and Stand for Justice is now open to anyone the federal system has run over. January 6 families aren't going anywhere. They're still with us. They're just no longer the only ones we can help. Yesterday, I mailed the letter that opens this new chapter. It went to the Office of the Pardon Attorney at the U.S. Department of Justice. It's about a man named Dr. Michael Rimlawi. His patients call him Dr. Mike. Dr. Mike is a spine surgeon from Dallas. For twenty years, people came to him when they couldn't sit through a workday, couldn't pick up their kids, couldn't sleep through the night. He did the small-incision kind of spine surgery. Less cutting, less blood, and most patients home the same day or the next. Then the federal government went after the hospital where he operated. Forest Park Medical Center paid a marketing firm to advertise its surgeons, something hospitals all over this country do every day. Prosecutors called it a kickback. Dr. Mike wasn't charged with hurting a patient. He wasn't charged with billing for a surgery that never happened. A jury convicted him in 2019. In 2021, a federal judge sentenced him to 90 months in prison, seven and a half years, and ordered him to pay $28,839,201.68 in restitution. To insurance companies. The Supreme Court refused to hear his case. Justice Gorsuch wrote that he would have heard it, because a judge, not a jury, set that $28.8 million. Dr. Mike did his time. He's home now with his wife and their two young sons. But unless something changes, that debt follows him for twenty years after his release. And a pardon alone won't erase it. The pardon has to say so. So our letter asks for two things: a full pardon, and that the pardon wipe out every dollar of restitution he hasn't paid. Patriot, Dr. Mike was nowhere near the Capitol. But if you've followed what happened to January 6 families, you already know this story. A prosecution built to make an example. A sentence that ends on paper and keeps going in real life. Restitution that follows a man home and sits at his kitchen table. Different courtroom. Same pattern. That's why Dr. Mike is the first story we're telling from the new Stand for Justice. He won't be the last. Please give $10, $35, $50, or whatever you can today to help us stand with him and with the next person who calls us. We seal records, go after fines and restitution that never should have been taken, and put our name on letters like the one I mailed yesterday. We do it for January 6 families, and now we can do it for people like Dr. Mike. If they can do this to a respected surgeon over a hospital's advertising budget, think about what they can do to a small business owner who never had a lawyer look at anything. Dr. Mike isn't asking anyone to feel sorry for him. He's asking for a fair finish. So are we. One letter opened the door. Your gift today is what walks him through it. It’s Team Benson, and we wanted to reach out before you log off for the
weekend with an important question: What do you want to see from
Michigan’s next governor?

With less than 50 days until Jocelyn is inaugurated as Michigan’s 50th
governor, we want to hear what issues are on your mind, what you think are
the most pressing problems Michigan is facing, and the solutions you would
like to see from your governor. [ https://act.jocelynbenson.com/survey/111326_survey?refcode=email_111326_survey&t=1001&akid=2154%2E181023%2Ei610eY ]Will you please take a moment today and

[ https://act.jocelynbenson.com/survey/111326_survey?refcode=email_111326_survey&t=1002&akid=2154%2E181023%2Ei610eY ]Weigh In →

Our historic win last Tuesday didn’t happen by luck. It was the result of
over a year of hard work from thousands of
supporters just
like you knocking doors, calling their neighbors, or chipping in a buck or
two, because they believed in the Michigan we were fighting for.

Now, the hard work begins.

It’s time to build that Michigan. The only way we can make a Michigan
where everyone can stay and thrive is by centering the issues affecting
everyday Michiganders.

Jocelyn has spent her entire career ensuring that every voice, every vote,
and every opinion has the right to be heard, counted, and respected.
That’s the exact kind of leadership she will bring to the governor’s
office — but the only way is if we hear from you.

That’s why we’re asking you to please fill out our Pre-Inauguration
Priorities Survey today and let us know your thoughts. It will take less
than a minute of your time, but goes a long way in delivering real results
for Michiganders.

Thank you,
Team Benson

name: The Eagle Dispatch
subject: Your cheap gas is sitting one headline away from gone
body:
Why the best part of this year’s inflation story just got fragile. | | [View in browser](https://theeagledispatch.podia.com/newsletters/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsibWVzc2FnZSI6Ik16TXhOalE0TUE9PSIsImV4cCI6bnVsbCwicHVyIjoibmV3c2xldHRlciJ9fQ--c7f6a17d0ef94d9ed00cd324f6bb6af8e23628f62701ce01a08b0810dee78c9e/preview?untrackable=true)
---
| | # [Your cheap gas is sitting one headline away from gone](https://theeagledispatch.podia.com/p/l/eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJuZXdzbGV0dGVyX2xpbmtfaWQiOjQ2MzI0NjR9._i_4jaXV4BJ3ZTjSseLy9xVYjW8Yxm2yPkVVZtVQjz0/eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJzdHVkZW50X2lkIjo2NjAzOTM5OSwibmV3c2xldHRlcl9pZCI6MzMxNjQ4MH0.m932AYPYyvf-XMz3buubkrB5yECRUP-EkmLmQ8aGAQw)
---
|
---
#### **The Oil Jolt**
## **One Truth Social post put the risk back into the oil price**
_Gas had been getting cheaper for weeks. A single line about Iran reminded the market how fast that can turn._
Oil had been the good-news story of the autumn. For weeks, every trip to the gas station cost a little less than the last. Then the President changed the mood in a single sentence.
---
On Thursday, Donald Trump wrote on Truth Social that the United States no longer needs a deal with Iran, saying Washington controls its money and the Strait of Hormuz. Oil jumped on the words alone. Brent crude [briefly touched $96 a barrel](https://theeagledispatch.podia.com/p/l/eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJuZXdzbGV0dGVyX2xpbmtfaWQiOjQ2MzI0NDB9.Ha-5cRR1P3h1wjJUc22PCXZqxVppD7Q83xnF6SNJwi4/eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJzdHVkZW50X2lkIjo2NjAzOTM5OSwibmV3c2xldHRlcl9pZCI6MzMxNjQ4MH0.m932AYPYyvf-XMz3buubkrB5yECRUP-EkmLmQ8aGAQw), up about 3.7 percent, and U.S. crude settled near $88.74.
That is this market in a nutshell right now. Physical supply has actually improved, with Saudi output up sharply, yet the ships still move through a narrow channel under threat, so a single [remark about Iran](https://theeagledispatch.podia.com/p/l/eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJuZXdzbGV0dGVyX2xpbmtfaWQiOjQ2MzI0NTB9.srkTBk0ZNoRBAa0JtuV5Eu8CMn4naJ93GpMxzTRrx-Q/eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJzdHVkZW50X2lkIjo2NjAzOTM5OSwibmV3c2xldHRlcl9pZCI6MzMxNjQ4MH0.m932AYPYyvf-XMz3buubkrB5yECRUP-EkmLmQ8aGAQw) can swing the price more than a tanker of real barrels.
Here is why it reaches your wallet. Brent had fallen about 25 percent from its late-October high near $118 as traders bet the war was ending, and that slide is what has been pulling prices down at the pump.
Thursday put a floor back under crude. It does not mean pump pain arrives tomorrow. The national average for gas had slipped toward $3.90 a gallon, a genuine break for households staring down winter heating bills. It is a reminder that the cheapest part of this year's inflation story sits one headline away from reversing, and I keep a close eye on oil for exactly that reason.
---
#### **Risk Comes Off**
## **As oil climbed, the riskier corners of the market cracked**
The same week that put a bid under oil took the air out of almost everything speculative. Bonds, crypto and stocks all slid the same direction at once, which rarely happens on a calm day. Money moved toward safety, and the move was not gentle.
---
▪ The 10-year Treasury yield pushed back toward 5 percent as a hot inflation signal and a near-certain December rate hike [roiled the bond market](https://theeagledispatch.podia.com/p/l/eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJuZXdzbGV0dGVyX2xpbmtfaWQiOjQ2MzI0NTh9.UQ8NcNcMEI359ye0n6cWsVxzDmiV4h2pHAuStpMoR5U/eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJzdHVkZW50X2lkIjo2NjAzOTM5OSwibmV3c2xldHRlcl9pZCI6MzMxNjQ4MH0.m932AYPYyvf-XMz3buubkrB5yECRUP-EkmLmQ8aGAQw).
▪ Bitcoin broke below $70,000 for the first time since August, down about 6 percent, and its fear gauge sank to the lowest reading in months as skittish money fled anything speculative.
▪ Stocks drifted lower across the board, the S&P 500 and Nasdaq each off about 0.4 percent, and the fear gauge jumped nearly 7 percent.
▪ The dollar firmed to a 19-month high, the mirror image of all that nervousness: when people want safety, they buy dollars.
None of this is a stampede. It is the market repricing risk in a single session, and the cash that sat still through it came out looking wise.
---
#### **One Number**
**3.75 million** is the annual pace of existing-home sales in October, [down 5.5 percent](https://theeagledispatch.podia.com/p/l/eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJuZXdzbGV0dGVyX2xpbmtfaWQiOjQ2MzI0NjJ9.T2rXJpyo7PktVJpsuwbRJzMRs6nvWzUvQV-J5zA3mlE/eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJzdHVkZW50X2lkIjo2NjAzOTM5OSwibmV3c2xldHRlcl9pZCI6MzMxNjQ4MH0.m932AYPYyvf-XMz3buubkrB5yECRUP-EkmLmQ8aGAQw) from September and among the slowest readings in years. High mortgage rates have simply priced a lot of buyers out, and owners who locked in cheap loans years ago will not trade them for a roughly 7 percent one today. A frozen resale market is its own kind of drag: fewer moves for new jobs, grown kids staying home longer, and a whole chain of movers and lenders and furniture stores all still waiting on a thaw that higher-for-longer rates keep pushing further off.
#### **Why I Led Here**
In the Army I spent years moving fuel, and the lesson that stuck was that it is rarely the size of the supply that undoes you. It is the width of the road it has to travel. A whole operation can run on one bridge, and the other side always knows which one.
The Strait of Hormuz is that bridge for the world's oil, and Thursday was a reminder that it still is. I led with energy because it is the one price that reaches everyone the same week, in the tank and in the grocery aisle, whatever the Fed does. A savings account does not care who runs Tehran, but a tank of gas does, and so does the furnace. The war looks close to over. The chokepoint is not going anywhere.
|

|
---
| _When the world moves, hold your ground._

clean_body: Why the best part of this year’s inflation story just got fragile. | | | | # | The Oil Jolt One Truth Social post put the risk back into the oil price Gas had been getting cheaper for weeks. A single line about Iran reminded the market how fast that can turn. Oil had been the good-news story of the autumn. For weeks, every trip to the gas station cost a little less than the last. Then the President changed the mood in a single sentence. On Thursday, Donald Trump wrote on Truth Social that the United States no longer needs a deal with Iran, saying Washington controls its money and the Strait of Hormuz. Oil jumped on the words alone. Brent crude , up about 3.7 percent, and U.S. crude settled near $88.74. That is this market in a nutshell right now. Physical supply has actually improved, with Saudi output up sharply, yet the ships still move through a narrow channel under threat, so a single can swing the price more than a tanker of real barrels. Here is why it reaches your wallet. Brent had fallen about 25 percent from its late-October high near $118 as traders bet the war was ending, and that slide is what has been pulling prices down at the pump. Thursday put a floor back under crude. It does not mean pump pain arrives tomorrow. The national average for gas had slipped toward $3.90 a gallon, a genuine break for households staring down winter heating bills. It is a reminder that the cheapest part of this year's inflation story sits one headline away from reversing, and I keep a close eye on oil for exactly that reason. Risk Comes Off As oil climbed, the riskier corners of the market cracked The same week that put a bid under oil took the air out of almost everything speculative. Bonds, crypto and stocks all slid the same direction at once, which rarely happens on a calm day. Money moved toward safety, and the move was not gentle. ▪ The 10-year Treasury yield pushed back toward 5 percent as a hot inflation signal and a near-certain December rate hike . ▪ Bitcoin broke below $70,000 for the first time since August, down about 6 percent, and its fear gauge sank to the lowest reading in months as skittish money fled anything speculative. ▪ Stocks drifted lower across the board, the S&P 500 and Nasdaq each off about 0.4 percent, and the fear gauge jumped nearly 7 percent. ▪ The dollar firmed to a 19-month high, the mirror image of all that nervousness: when people want safety, they buy dollars. None of this is a stampede. It is the market repricing risk in a single session, and the cash that sat still through it came out looking wise. One Number 3.75 million is the annual pace of existing-home sales in October, from September and among the slowest readings in years. High mortgage rates have simply priced a lot of buyers out, and owners who locked in cheap loans years ago will not trade them for a roughly 7 percent one today. A frozen resale market is its own kind of drag: fewer moves for new jobs, grown kids staying home longer, and a whole chain of movers and lenders and furniture stores all still waiting on a thaw that higher-for-longer rates keep pushing further off. Why I Led Here In the Army I spent years moving fuel, and the lesson that stuck was that it is rarely the size of the supply that undoes you. It is the width of the road it has to travel. A whole operation can run on one bridge, and the other side always knows which one. The Strait of Hormuz is that bridge for the world's oil, and Thursday was a reminder that it still is. I led with energy because it is the one price that reaches everyone the same week, in the tank and in the grocery aisle, whatever the Fed does. A savings account does not care who runs Tehran, but a tank of gas does, and so does the furnace. The war looks close to over. The chokepoint is not going anywhere. | | | When the world moves, hold your ground. | | 3500 Lenox Road, Suite 625, Atlanta, GA 30326 | "Unsubscribe"

_Already a paid subscriber? Then like, share, and keep showing up in the comments. It matters more than you know._
* * *
I remain in awe of how little the Republican Party has learned from last week's election.
They lost Mississippi. _Mississippi._ And if you turn on Fox News right now, you're likely to see them talking about migrant caravans again, the same tired tactic they pull out every time they're in trouble. Donald Trump is going on podcasts and addressing spewing irrelevant nonsense, arguing that the Cleveland Guardians need to change their name back to the Indians. Yes, that's real. He's still telling everyone it's the golden age of America. He's still arguing that provoking a war with Iran was the right decision.
Meanwhile, Americans are struggling to afford groceries, health care, and housing. Health insurance premiums are facing another year of double-digit increases, and families in Kansas City just spent weeks terrified that their children could lose in-network access to Children's Mercy Hospital. It took a public outcry before the hospital reached a deal with even one ACA insurer for next year.
And Donald Trump is out there telling everyone it's all A-Okay.
That's been the theme of my week, because this work keeps me running headfirst into it. I've been going on right-wing media to debate these people, and I've been talking, offscreen, with others working on the right. Not one of them seems to have the slightest understanding of why they lost, nor are they even willing to address it. That shouldn't surprise anyone, because I've been saying for two years that they never understood why they won in 2024 either.
Americans weren't handing Trump a blank check to pursue every grievance he'd ever had. They were demanding change. They wanted relief from the cost of living, a government that worked, and leaders who actually gave a damn about the problems they were facing. Trump promised them that change. Republicans apparently convinced themselves that meant voters had embraced everything else that came along with him. Republicans mistook that opportunity for a blank check. And now they're play-acting shock that Americans are holding them accountable.
There's no real debate on their side, no fire, no desire to take the party in a different direction. Maybe it's happening behind closed doors, but I'm not seeing them from Republican leaders, conservative commentators, or anyone they're putting forward as the future of the party. It's the same people, the same arguments, and the same refusal to admit that they have played a part in the downfall of their party.
They're treating 2026 like a fluke, like the stars aligned for the Democrats, like we stole a bunch of races we had no business winning, and everything will snap back into place in a few years. I don't buy it. I think there's a real chance we're watching an actual realignment, that we're watching people finally understand how much Donald Trump and the Republican Party are hurting them.
And instead of reckoning with what voters just told them, they're doubling down in every possible way.
They gave us Jim Jordan as Speaker of the House, a conservative more unlikable than Mike Johnson. They gave us more Stephen Miller, which equals Trump deciding he's going to keep doing the same shit, especially when it comes to harassing immigrant communities and perpetuating violence on Americans.
* * *

We need to fight for higher wages, affordable healthcare, an end to corporate price gouging, and a government that works for working class people instead of the wealthy and powerful. That's the work we're committed to at Endless Urgency. Paid subscribers are what make that possible. * * *
It's the same people, the same policies, and the same dumb political obsessions. The voters change their minds, but Republican leaders seemingly see no reason to change theirs.
They've learned nothing. That means this realignment could carry right into 2028. Even in a presidential year. Even with higher turnout. We might not be able to win Mississippi in a presidential year. But we can absolutely win the presidency.
Here's the thing, though: Republicans aren't the only ones misreading Tuesday.
I'm in Denver this week at the Democratic conference, and yesterday I heard a prominent Democratic politician give a speech about how America is back now that Democrats have won. I sat there thinking: No. Not even close. America is a long way from being back. Democrats have to understand that we are not a popular party, and that we won't be until we deliver on the material needs of the working class.
Republicans are already out there bragging about how they're going to obstruct everything Democrats want to do. Fine. Let them. We still need to do those things anyway. We need to be seen trying. We need to be aggressive at the federal level, and at the state and local level too, to improve people's lives, because this country is spiraling out of control. People need to see that government can work for them.
When Republicans stop us, we go straight to the American people and say: give us a Democratic president. Give us more Democratic senators. Let us break the filibuster, move this country forward, and make a real difference in your life.
Or we can keep going with Republicans. Those who are screaming about trans kids for the thousandth time, making up shit about migrant caravans, trying to convince you that your life is good and that you should be more grateful to Donald Trump for the economy he built us.
That's the choice. We make them own their record: the destruction of the economy, this illegal war, the corruption, the lies, everything Americans are furious about. At the same time, we must show that we have fresh ideas, that we can improve people's lives, and that government can be a force for good.
And the ideas don't have to be complicated. I've been pushing single-issue bills for a while now, and I'll keep pushing them. Raise the minimum wage. That's one bill. Bring back the healthcare subsidies. That's another. Go after surveillance pricing, which is crushing Americans right now. That's a third. No giant omnibus packages. No 2,000-page bills nobody can explain. _Just one clear fight after another, every single day._
People need to understand that we're fighting for them, passing legislation every day, against a group of people who don't care about them and don't have the decency to listen when they send a message like they did on Tuesday.
The American people sent a booming message to the Republican Party. I don't know what the Democratic equivalent of losing Mississippi would be, but if it ever happened, you can be damn sure it would send a chill down my spine. I'd be up at night figuring out how we screwed up.
These guys? Not so much.
With urgency,
--Mike

# **[Scott Bessent blindsides Lutnick in Situation Room over China chip leak](https://substack.com/redirect/eaf7d7bb-02ca-403d-ab3f-1d0c7511331b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
Treasury Secretary **[Scott Bessent confronted Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick in the Situation Room](https://substack.com/redirect/e4583be1-e028-45d6-b6ad-72dcd3e761d2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** over why Nvidia customer Megaspeed remained off the Entity List despite repeated approvals.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/eaf7d7bb-02ca-403d-ab3f-1d0c7511331b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Situation Room exchange** : Bessent asked why Megaspeed was not listed; Lutnick stammered and said he did not know and would look into it.
* **Repeated stalling** : Axios sources said Trump approved action on three occasions in May, August, and Nov. 5, but Lutnick delayed each time.
* **Oval Office push** : The **[group moved to the Oval,](https://substack.com/redirect/1401a497-f899-4016-8546-0601b369159d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** Trump called Musk who sided with controls, and Trump said "Let's get it done," yet Lutnick later proposed more options.

| 1:18 PM * Nov 13, 2026 * 45.5K Views27 Replies * 118 Reposts * 447 Likes
---](https://substack.com/redirect/4c035500-6a81-4b04-898d-2a74c9b6c1f4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* **Denial and probes** : A Commerce spokesperson denied the confrontation; Kessler reportedly halted a Megaspeed probe after Nvidia contact, and DOJ has taken over related investigations.
* **Aides blame inaction** : Trump aides **[pointed to Lutnick over failure to act](https://substack.com/redirect/2bf1c5ec-90a7-4fd8-adde-fda2cac1c0eb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** on diversion concerns despite earlier approvals.
* **Chip volume large** : Megaspeed has purchased **[more than 4.8 billion dollars of advanced Nvidia chips](https://substack.com/redirect/47c98a89-ec1b-4361-8626-de177b1ce9d0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** since June 2024, according to a Democratic letter.
* **Voluntary testimony** : Lutnick a**[greed to appear before the Senate Banking Committee](https://substack.com/redirect/8717eb03-672e-4233-979c-f931c60a1c14?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** as the chip-sales scrutiny intensified.

# [Global Microsoft outage drags into Friday as recovery still stalled](https://substack.com/redirect/eaf7d7bb-02ca-403d-ab3f-1d0c7511331b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
A **[global Microsoft outage continued Friday,](https://substack.com/redirect/820156c0-fb50-4b73-9198-e4cece4d4419?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** weighing on the stock as traders also digested the Nvidia leadership change and inflation data.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/eaf7d7bb-02ca-403d-ab3f-1d0c7511331b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Second-day impact** : The disruption left **[Microsoft shares down roughly 2.7 percent](https://substack.com/redirect/7f5b828b-4057-412a-8b33-6b86f28d0327?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** in early trading.
* **Broader tape mixed** : Futures rose overall but the outage added pressure on large-cap tech alongside the Nvidia story.
* **Recovery efforts** : Reports noted ongoing work to restore services for thousands of users.
* **Market focus split** : Traders balanced the outage against the cooler PPI print and Nvidia stabilization.

# [Nvidia plunge drags indexes lower as AI trade cracks](https://substack.com/redirect/eaf7d7bb-02ca-403d-ab3f-1d0c7511331b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Major U.S. indexes closed lower Thursday **[after Nvidia's leadership shock sent shares plunging](https://substack.com/redirect/7e16f36b-a6db-4a41-837d-0d569ee26808?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** at the open, though dip buyers limited the damage by the close.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/eaf7d7bb-02ca-403d-ab3f-1d0c7511331b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**Open plunge severe** : Nvidia fell as much as 14 percent early, pulling the Nasdaq and S&P 500 lower **[before partial recovery.](https://substack.com/redirect/820156c0-fb50-4b73-9198-e4cece4d4419?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
**Close losses modest** : The Dow, S&P 500 and Nasdaq each finished down about 0.4 percent as the market digested the exit and higher yields.
**Rotation visible** : **[Cash moved into other chip and AI names](https://substack.com/redirect/aa0a1c0d-3901-422a-b2f7-32b374816ac7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** while small caps, biotechs and defense lagged.
**Futures rebound Friday** : Early **[Friday futures rose](https://substack.com/redirect/f392b483-c125-4c9c-8851-9d5dc33de276?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** as traders looked past the shock toward a cooler producer-price reading.
[Subscribe](https://substack.com/redirect/5d62fa17-c2bc-4671-94bb-e8c16b432268?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
# [Democrats demand records as Huang agrees to testify](https://substack.com/redirect/eaf7d7bb-02ca-403d-ab3f-1d0c7511331b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Senators Elizabeth Warren and Chris Coons told officials to **[preserve every record of administration contacts with Jensen Huang](https://substack.com/redirect/2fa0db0e-eeec-40a5-8b15-b57226145af7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/2fa0db0e-eeec-40a5-8b15-b57226145af7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)by Nov. 17 as Congress prepares hearings.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/eaf7d7bb-02ca-403d-ab3f-1d0c7511331b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Preserve directive** : The letter seeks call transcripts, China-trip memos and details of the halted Megaspeed probe, with written confirmation required.
* **Spy status open** : Attorney General Todd Blanche[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/15b86f1d-3520-4e88-8039-8bbe0d7ca736?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[said neither DOJ nor FBI has confirmed](https://substack.com/redirect/15b86f1d-3520-4e88-8039-8bbe0d7ca736?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** whether Alice Huang was a spy, though an investigation continues.
* **Huang to appear** : The former CEO has agreed to testify before Congress ahead of Thanksgiving on the relationship and chip issues.
* **Scrutiny widens** : Lawmakers are **[examining what the administration knew about the affair](https://substack.com/redirect/47c98a89-ec1b-4361-8626-de177b1ce9d0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** and any export-control implications.

[Subscribe](https://substack.com/redirect/5d62fa17-c2bc-4671-94bb-e8c16b432268?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
# [Huang called her a deer in the headlights. Now Kress runs Nvidia](https://substack.com/redirect/eaf7d7bb-02ca-403d-ab3f-1d0c7511331b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Interim CEO **[Colette Kress takes charge of Nvidia](https://substack.com/redirect/f70ea36e-b16a-4a0e-8c34-236a5982ac7c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** after Huang **[previously belittled her dealmaking skills](https://substack.com/redirect/3d516679-46d8-42e2-930a-1771b4b86345?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/3d516679-46d8-42e2-930a-1771b4b86345?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)at a summer meeting, according to reporting on the leadership handoff.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/eaf7d7bb-02ca-403d-ab3f-1d0c7511331b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Long finance tenure** : **[Kress has served as CFO](https://substack.com/redirect/1d4016be-2347-4d22-ae49-ae1980405c23?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** since 2013 after earlier roles at Cisco and Microsoft and holds substantial Nvidia equity.
* **Board chair shift** : Harvey Jones, a director since 1993, becomes the company's first board chair as the search for a permanent chief begins.
* **Internal skepticism** : Huang had questioned some of her deal decisions and **[described her as a deer in the headlights,](https://substack.com/redirect/534975d1-0e7d-4066-b214-611374dcf16e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** the Wall Street Journal reported.
* **Employee note** : Kress and Jones thanked staff for resilience and dedication in an email after the resignation.

[Subscribe](https://substack.com/redirect/5d62fa17-c2bc-4671-94bb-e8c16b432268?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
# [AI financing bet tested without Huang at Nvidia](https://substack.com/redirect/eaf7d7bb-02ca-403d-ab3f-1d0c7511331b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Jensen Huang's exit puts the roughly 500 billion dollar[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/a8b8ed03-8116-4282-bb36-7bbee00ebf70?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[AI financing vision and related circular deals](https://substack.com/redirect/a8b8ed03-8116-4282-bb36-7bbee00ebf70?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** under new scrutiny as investors watch whether support continues under interim leadership.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/eaf7d7bb-02ca-403d-ab3f-1d0c7511331b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Chip-to-debt plan** : Huang had **[promoted turning AI processors into tradable securities;](https://substack.com/redirect/d5dea444-05d2-4651-af21-db7c76e044ea?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** the transition raises questions about follow-through.
* **Neocloud exposure** : Nvidia has backed parts of the buildout through investments, commercial commitments and supplier relationships that a new chief may limit.
* **Circular structure** : Reporting described Nvidia funding landlords, backstopping tenants and selling chips into the same ecosystem.
* **Kress test** : The interim CEO now oversees the web of commitments while the permanent search continues.

[Subscribe](https://substack.com/redirect/5d62fa17-c2bc-4671-94bb-e8c16b432268?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
# [Goldman still sees S&P 500 at 8,700 next year](https://substack.com/redirect/eaf7d7bb-02ca-403d-ab3f-1d0c7511331b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Goldman Sachs **[forecasts the S&P 500 reaching 8,700](https://substack.com/redirect/8be027e9-c96e-4b0b-b4c7-117b7f6366c3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** within a year[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/8610f383-ddd9-4b46-bc88-73b84ac6a8df?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[even as it expects slower earnings growth](https://substack.com/redirect/8610f383-ddd9-4b46-bc88-73b84ac6a8df?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** and residual risks after the recent selloff.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/eaf7d7bb-02ca-403d-ab3f-1d0c7511331b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Valuation support** : **[Strategists pointed to cheaper multiples](https://substack.com/redirect/c2b8b8cb-6244-4d66-8451-35a48e585c1d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** following the pullback as a reason the bull case remains intact.
* **Hyperscaler view** : The firm reportedly sees AI hyperscalers as relatively defensive after the tech rout.
* **Upside estimate** : One framing put the potential advance near 14 percent over the next 12 months.
* **Risks acknowledged** : The call includes slower profit growth and possible volatility along the path to the target.

[Subscribe](https://substack.com/redirect/5d62fa17-c2bc-4671-94bb-e8c16b432268?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
# ["Bring back THE Boss": Nvidia staff petition for Huang return](https://substack.com/redirect/eaf7d7bb-02ca-403d-ab3f-1d0c7511331b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Some Nvidia staff have **[urged the board to consider bringing Jensen Huang back,](https://substack.com/redirect/e787a346-1509-4e3e-ba05-b76b797cc4e4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/e787a346-1509-4e3e-ba05-b76b797cc4e4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)while prediction markets weigh internal candidates and **[even divorce odds](https://substack.com/redirect/a5113f37-ad55-479b-ad9c-c899fa9ae7f4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** after the resignation.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/eaf7d7bb-02ca-403d-ab3f-1d0c7511331b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Internal post** : An employee message asking the board to weigh staff views and reinstate Huang gathered more than 1,600 comments.
* **Kalshi odds** : Traders on Kalshi have speculated that longtime executive Ian Buck could replace Huang as CEO.
* **Buck candidacy** : Piper Sandler floated Buck, a **[22-year veteran leading hyperscaler and high-performance computing,](https://substack.com/redirect/f8ef48c7-8371-40c3-b6db-66e59a49107d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** as a strong internal option.
* **Divorce pricing** : Prediction markets put the chance of a Huang divorce near 37 percent amid the scandal coverage.

Peter, we just got through an incredibly fruitful, incredibly demanding election season. It’s natural to want to take a breather. But we still have to defend democracy from attacks on multiple fronts, including:
1. New gerrymanders that GOP lawmakers could pass in lame-duck sessions before they leave office in January. (Looking at you, Texas!)
2. Attempts to undermine the census and kick off a new wave of manipulated maps based on skewed population counts.
3. Ongoing, relentless, desperate attempts to restrict the right to vote.

Attorney General Eric Holder’s post-election words help inspire us to stay in the fight: | [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/143411603/660120883/1548394306?refcode=don_ndrc_tier1_email_TwoPathsForward_email_20261112-NDRC-Tier1-TwoPathsForward_&utm_source=email&utm_medium=email&utm_term=don&utm_content=20261112-NDRC-Tier1-TwoPathsForward_&utm_campaign=TwoPathsForward&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxMy8xLzg5Mjk0IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjdlZThjZGQ4LTk1ZGYtZjExMS05MWYwLTAwMGQzYTE4ZTI0NCIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=m5s4Z6A1V9w3ROb2H4VqVun10aNSwq61DC4oCVJhlbY=)

Open enrollment is underway, and new federal healthcare changes could affect your coverage and costs.
| | [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/143411697/660121211/-1405467182?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDEvMS82MTY0NSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIxMDViZTA4Yi05NmRmLWYxMTEtOTFmMC0wMDBkM2ExOGUyNDQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=crEeSeB64OHmC45-58TpkXbl9Zfz2Cct8fGGOuMEiaw=&emci=5efdb2ea-bfde-f111-91f0-000d3a18e244&emdi=105be08b-96df-f111-91f0-000d3a18e244&ceid=14565883)
---

| | Welcome back to Fact Friday. Open enrollment for 2027 health insurance coverage is underway, and whether you're enrolling for the first time or renewing an existing plan, there are some important changes you should know about. **FACT #1: Healthcare premiums are continuing to rise.** According to KFF, benchmark Affordable Care Act (ACA) Marketplace premiums are increasing by an average of 13% nationally for 2027, following a 26% increase in 2026. Combined with the expiration of enhanced tax credits, many local families will see higher monthly costs even if they still qualify for standard financial assistance. **FACT #2: Some lawfully present immigrants will lose access to financial assistance.** Beginning January 1, 2027, new federal restrictions will eliminate ACA Marketplace subsidies for many lawfully present immigrants, including certain refugees and asylees, potentially leaving them responsible for the full cost of coverage. **FACT #3: Changes to premium tax credits could affect your tax filings.** Starting with 2026 tax filings, federal law eliminated limits on how much excess premium tax credit assistance households must repay. If your income ends up higher than projected when you sign up, you could owe more when filing your taxes in 2027. **If you or your family need health insurance for 2027, here are two important deadlines:**
* December 15, 2026: Last day to enroll for coverage beginning January 1, 2027.
* January 15, 2027: Final day to enroll in or change Marketplace coverage for 2027. Coverage selected after December 15 generally begins February 1.

Even if you're already enrolled, I encourage you to review your options, compare plans, and check whether you still qualify for financial assistance before automatic renewal kicks in. **Healthcare is a necessity, not a luxury. No one should have to choose between getting the medical care they need and keeping up with their monthly bills.** If you want to keep getting clear, fact-based breakdowns of the issues affecting our community, make sure you stay connected and share this with someone who should be paying attention, too. clean_body: Open enrollment is underway, and new federal healthcare changes could affect your coverage and costs. | | | | Welcome back to Fact Friday. Open enrollment for 2027 health insurance coverage is underway, and whether you're enrolling for the first time or renewing an existing plan, there are some important changes you should know about. FACT #1: Healthcare premiums are continuing to rise. According to KFF, benchmark Affordable Care Act (ACA) Marketplace premiums are increasing by an average of 13% nationally for 2027, following a 26% increase in 2026. Combined with the expiration of enhanced tax credits, many local families will see higher monthly costs even if they still qualify for standard financial assistance. FACT #2: Some lawfully present immigrants will lose access to financial assistance. Beginning January 1, 2027, new federal restrictions will eliminate ACA Marketplace subsidies for many lawfully present immigrants, including certain refugees and asylees, potentially leaving them responsible for the full cost of coverage. FACT #3: Changes to premium tax credits could affect your tax filings. Starting with 2026 tax filings, federal law eliminated limits on how much excess premium tax credit assistance households must repay. If your income ends up higher than projected when you sign up, you could owe more when filing your taxes in 2027. If you or your family need health insurance for 2027, here are two important deadlines: December 15, 2026: Last day to enroll for coverage beginning January 1, 2027. January 15, 2027: Final day to enroll in or change Marketplace coverage for 2027. Coverage selected after December 15 generally begins February 1. Even if you're already enrolled, I encourage you to review your options, compare plans, and check whether you still qualify for financial assistance before automatic renewal kicks in. Healthcare is a necessity, not a luxury. No one should have to choose between getting the medical care they need and keeping up with their monthly bills. If you want to keep getting clear, fact-based breakdowns of the issues affecting our community, make sure you stay connected and share this with someone who should be paying attention, too. Staying informed is power. Let's use it, El Paso. ---
| | | [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/143412833/660124934/-1469492719?refcode=EM_F_261114MS_N_LS_90DO_11_NG_N_Logo&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAwNy8xLzg4NDk1IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjUwNzkxMWJhLTlhZGYtZjExMS05MWYwLTAwMGQzYTE4ZTI0NCIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=dI7mqkqrk4KxDqjz_6QprVUG7CWXqHinTEANcGIsy3g=)
---
Peter,

It’s official: Mississippi elected its first Black senator since 1881 (Congratulations, Democrat Scott Colom!). It’s clear that this historically tough state for women and democrats is ready for change, and now is the time to keep up that momentum.

**Here’s how Her Bold Move thinks about this: Mississippi is ranked at the very bottom in the nation (48th out of 50) for women’s representation in its government.** At this moment, women only account for 9 members out of 52 in the State Senate, and 18 out of 122 in the State House. That’s only 15.5% of the entire state legislature.

And, unfortunately, it shows: **Mississippi has one of the strictest abortion bans in the nation, and many other troubling laws for women.**

[**_We know you’re short on time. You can support our efforts to elect MORE WOMEN in MISSISSIPPI in 2027 and beyond by chipping in $5 or more TODAY! →_**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/143412834/660124935/-1469492719?refcode=EM_F_261114MS_N_LS_90DO_11_NG_N_L1&amount=5&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAwNy8xLzg4NDk1IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjUwNzkxMWJhLTlhZGYtZjExMS05MWYwLTAwMGQzYTE4ZTI0NCIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=dI7mqkqrk4KxDqjz_6QprVUG7CWXqHinTEANcGIsy3g=)

**Now, the numbers are about to get even worse. In Mississippi in 2023...**
* 82% of the State House races were unopposed.
* 73% of the State Senate races were completely unchallenged.
* **That means Mississippi has one of the highest rates of unopposed elections in the country.**
* Mississippi remains the only state in U.S. history that has _never sent a woman to the U.S. House of Representatives._

In 2027, Mississippi will be holding elections for ALL 122 State House seats and ALL 52 State Senate Seats, along with other statewide (including Governor) and local elections. We owe it to the women of Mississippi to help them gain better representation in their state, and that’s why we’re reaching out.

Hi friend, Last week, Sherrod Brown was elected to the U.S. Senate, and Amy Acton became the first woman elected governor of Ohio. This is an incredible win for two candidates who ran great campaigns on an uneven playing field. **Even after Republicans redrew Ohio’s district maps and flooded the airwaves with super PAC-funded lies, Ohio voters could not be silenced.** They showed up to the polls and chose decency over cruelty, fairness over corruption, and responsibility over chaos. clean_body: Congratulations to Sherrod and Amy for their incredible wins. To unsubscribe, | | Hi friend, Last week, Sherrod Brown was elected to the U.S. Senate, and Amy Acton became the first woman elected governor of Ohio. This is an incredible win for two candidates who ran great campaigns on an uneven playing field. Even after Republicans redrew Ohio’s district maps and flooded the airwaves with super PAC-funded lies, Ohio voters could not be silenced. They showed up to the polls and chose decency over cruelty, fairness over corruption, and responsibility over chaos. That’s the kind of leadership Ohioans deserve — and it’s what Sherrod and Amy will deliver. Congratulations to them both. I’m thrilled to work with them to strengthen Southwest Ohio and tackle the biggest challenges facing our communities. Now that the election is over, we have to stay focused on the work ahead: making it easier to afford a good and dignified life. | | | | Thank you.
---
It is the honor of my life to represent West Michigan in Congress, and I am so grateful to everyone who put their trust in me. Whether you live here or cheered us on from across the country, thank you so much for your support.
This campaign was not one of promises, but one of results. We cannot slogan our way out of the problems facing our country. We need leaders who will do the tough work to lower costs, expand access to care, and curb corruption. That's what I'll keep doing: leading from the pragmatic middle of the aisle, representing the middle of the country, and fighting for the middle class.
To our volunteers, campaign staff, supporters, and my friends and family, thank you for being part of this effort. I promise to do the very best that I can for our community and our country. God helping me, I won't let you down.
Gratefully,
Hillary Scholten 💙

Friends,
The past week has been an incredible whirlwind of excitement and hope for the future of the Hudson Valley and our country. I have been down in D.C. for new member orientation, and I am so excited about the work ahead to serve our community and deliver on lowering costs and rooting out corruption. Throughout the campaign, I said again and again that our representatives in Washington could learn a lesson from the brave men and women who risk their lives to defend our democracy. I truly believe that. To deliver real results, we _must_ put country over party. We _must_ put the people’s interests over our own self-interest. That’s precisely what I intend to do. I am grateful for everyone who put in the work to help us get to this point. I could not have done it without each and every one of you. I will forever carry the ethos of Duty, Honor, Country with me — from the hallowed halls of West Point to the halls of Congress. I can’t wait to get to work.
With gratitude and fire, Cait Conley

clean_body: | Welcome to the Indiana Democratic Party's weekly newsletter, The Kernel of Truth. The State Party will provide the most important facts - a kernel of truth - from the week. = ** Indiana Is Moving Toward Democrats, and the Map Shows It In just four years, Indiana has moved nearly 30 points toward Democrats. Every county in Indiana shifted toward Democrats. Sixteen counties also flipped to Democrats. In 2022, Democrats won three counties. In 2026, we won 19. Hoosiers are tired of the corruption with Republican leadership in Indiana; they want leaders who will focus on lowering the price of gas, healthcare, and utilities. This shift is a huge step forward in our state, but we can’t stop volunteering, organizing, and donating now. Let’s keep this momentum going for 2027 and 2028! Congressman-elect J.D. Ford’s Victory Considered One of the Biggest Upsets Nationally Congressman-elect J.D. Ford knows what it’s like to flip red seats. He did it in 2018 when he flipped a State Senate seat blue that had been strong Republican territory for decades. And now, he’s flipped the 5th Congressional District, defying the odds and the race ratings given by pundits across the country. This race was considered “Safe Republican” until just weeks before Election Day. This week, Time published, , and Indiana Rep.-elect J.D. Ford was considered one of the biggest upsets anywhere in the country on Election Night. The 5th Congressional District was won by Donald Trump by 17 percentage points in 2024, but never tell Congressman-elect Ford the odds. He worked hard by going to every county in the district, and moving each one more Democratic than 2020, 2022, and 2024. Each week, the State Party will highlight key policy or programs from Democrats at the Statehouse or across the state. Democrats deliver a better future for Hoosier families, and we urge you to share this information with your networks. A Very Happy Birthday to Secretary-elect Beau Bayh and Congressman-elect J.D. Ford! Happy belated birthday to two of Indiana’s Democratic leaders! Secretary of State-elect Beau Bayh on November 8th, and Congressman-elect J.D. Ford on November 6. Thank you both for everything you’ve done for Hoosier families. We can’t wait to see you continue to make Hoosiers proud in your new roles! We did it! Democrats just won back the House and the Senate, and I am fired up about what comes next.

Colorado lawmakers’ $1,000 internship comes with a religion and
ancestry test

Want the full news breakdown? Listen to the Mountain Minute podcast

[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

🏔️ HERE IN COLORADO... Gabriel Garcia, who police say killed a
Lakewood officer on an RTD bus, was on parole despite about 35 arrests
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.
Rep. Jeff Hurd survived the blue wave
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.
and will likely be Colorado’s lone Republican in Congress;
Democratic Socialist Melissa Mejía won an at-large Denver council
seat
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.
and Douglas County approved $5.95 million
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.
for Macanta Regional Park.

🇺🇸 ON THE NATIONAL STAGE... The House voted 211-204 to kill Rep.
Thomas Massie’s resolutions to impeach War Secretary Pete Hegseth
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.
after 11 Democrats, including Colorado’s Rep. Brittany Pettersen,
missed the vote; with all Democrats present, the effort would have
advanced.

🗣️ COMMENTARY SPOTLIGHT... Cory Gaines writes that fewer
operating wells are pushing orphan well fees higher
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.
Wayne Laugesen argues a Capitol internship limited to Muslim and
Middle Eastern, North African or South Asian applicants violates
anti-discrimination law
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.
Tim Meisburger questions the legitimacy of Democratic wins
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.
over voter ID; and Heidi Ganahl reports Arapahoe County’s board
chair ended public comment on election questions
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.
with “This conversation is over.”

This is your Mountain Minute for Friday, November 13, 2026.

– Team RMV

TODAY'S TOP STORIES

COLORADO LAWMAKERS’ $1,000 INTERNSHIP COMES WITH A RELIGION AND
ANCESTRY TEST
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

WAYNE'S WORD
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

_Imagine a sharp kid from Aurora. She has straight A’s, a weekend
job, and dreams of public service. Her parents came from Mexico.
She’s Catholic. She finds a flyer announcing a paid internship at
the state Capitol and reads the first requirement. She cries after
learning that her genetics, religion, and ethnic background are a
problem._

_She does not qualify. Not because of her grades, but for identity
traits she did not ask for and cannot change. In the United States, we
don’t limit opportunities based on family trees. Doing so would be
100% antithetical to the values of a country that won a civil war and
passed a federal civil rights act._

_To turn away a young woman because she’s of Mexican descent would
be a crime. Two Colorado legislators just committed that crime boldly
and for all to see — as if they are immune from American and
Colorado law. Colorado’s mainstream media hasn’t acknowledge this
disgrace._

READ MORE
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

“THIS CONVERSATION IS OVER”: ARAPAHOE COUNTY BOARD CHAIR SHUTS
DOWN RESIDENTS’ ELECTION QUESTIONS
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

BY HEIDI GANAHL, ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

_Arapahoe County residents asked commissioners to let losing
candidates compare paper ballots to machine counts; the board chair
told them “this conversation is over.”_

*
THIN MARGINS, NO ANSWERS: Arapahoe County voters rejected Propositions
134 and 135 by margins of just 2,411 and 4,900 votes, respectively,
while neighboring Douglas County approved Proposition 134 with 63%
support.

*
A MODEST ASK, REBUFFED: Candidate Annette Budd proposed letting each
candidate inspect ballots from one precinct against the cast vote
record without removing them from the warehouse; Board Chair Leslie
Summey instead told residents “I don’t have the authority” and
twice reminded them “you did not elect me.”

*
EVEN A FELLOW DEMOCRAT PUSHED BACK: Commissioner Rhonda Fields
reminded colleagues that speakers “need to be treated with respect
and dignity,” while Commissioner Jessica Campbell dismissed the
testimony as “nonfactual.”

MACANTA REGIONAL PARK: DOUGLAS COUNTY APPROVES $5.95 MILLION CONTRACT
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

BY SHAINA COLE | LOCAL | NOVEMBER 13

_A stretch of open land south of Crowfoot Valley Road in Douglas
County is getting trails, a trailhead and stairs built for a workout.
Douglas County commissioners approved a construction contract for
Macanta Regional Park at their Nov. 10 business meeting, according to
the county’s announcement._

COLORADO’S NEW SUPERMAJORITY: SIX LEGISLATORS SAY NEITHER PARTY IS
UNITED
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

BY SHAINA COLE | STATE | NOVEMBER 12

_Democrats hold two-thirds of both chambers of the Colorado
legislature, enough to put constitutional amendments on the ballot and
override a governor’s veto without a single Republican vote. Asked
what they intend to do with it, two of the three Democrats who
answered RMV said the caucus is not going to vote as one. Asked the
same questions, two Republicans said the same thing about theirs._

COLORADO VETERANS: FROM DACHAU TO CAMP HALE, 13 RESOLUTIONS AND A
MEMORIAL’S UNFINISHED LIST
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

BY SHAINA COLE | STATE | NOVEMBER 11

_On the morning of April 29, 1945, soldiers of the 157th Infantry
Regiment set foot inside Dachau. The 157th had Colorado National Guard
roots and fought as part of the U.S. Army’s 45th Infantry Division.
House Joint Resolution 26-1011 calls it the Colorado National
Guard’s 157th._

the Senator sitting in the last row on the Republican side near the
chamber's busiest entrance has maintained the official "Candy Desk."
Senators from across the aisle sneak sweets from the drawer during
long floor debates, and the desk's occupant typically stocks it with
treats from their home state.

| | | Peter, Voters demanded change last week. We must honor it. That’s why we’re calling on the incoming Democratic caucus **to support Senator Chris Van Hollen for Senate Majority Leader.** While we’re thankful for Senator Chuck Schumer’s decade of service, it’s time for a new generation of leadership. One that will deliver on housing, health care, and childcare for everyone. One that will take a bold stance against ICE’s lawlessness, and our never-ending funnel of money and arms to Israel. **Sen. Van Hollen has taken those stances, and more.** He’s a co-sponsor of the Medicare for All Act. He has been staunchly opposed to the out-of-control funding for ICE and DHS, and even flew to El Salvador to demand the return of Kilmar Abrego Garcia — a constituent who was wrongly deported by the Trump administration. And he was one of the earliest signers to try and block offensive weapons sales to the Israeli government. **We’re calling on every returning and newly elected Democratic senator to back Van Hollen,** and commit to the Working Families agenda that voters demanded last Tuesday. And to succeed, we need YOU to make your voices heard too. **Text LEADER to 30403 or[dial 833-636-3260 to call your Senators](tel:+18336363260), urging them to support Senator Chris Van Hollen as the next Senate Majority Leader. clean_body: | | | Peter, Voters demanded change last week. We must honor it. That’s why we’re calling on the incoming Democratic caucus to support Senator Chris Van Hollen for Senate Majority Leader. While we’re thankful for Senator Chuck Schumer’s decade of service, it’s time for a new generation of leadership. One that will deliver on housing, health care, and childcare for everyone. One that will take a bold stance against ICE’s lawlessness, and our never-ending funnel of money and arms to Israel. Sen. Van Hollen has taken those stances, and more. He’s a co-sponsor of the Medicare for All Act. He has been staunchly opposed to the out-of-control funding for ICE and DHS, and even flew to El Salvador to demand the return of Kilmar Abrego Garcia — a constituent who was wrongly deported by the Trump administration. And he was one of the earliest signers to try and block offensive weapons sales to the Israeli government. We’re calling on every returning and newly elected Democratic senator to back Van Hollen, and commit to the Working Families agenda that voters demanded last Tuesday. And to succeed, we need YOU to make your voices heard too. Text LEADER to 30403 ortel:+18336363260, urging them to support Senator Chris Van Hollen as the next Senate Majority Leader. We’ll suggest a script — all you need is a phone! tel:+18336363260 The people have given Democrats an opportunity to prove that they’re ready to meet this moment. No more sternly-worded letters. body:
Food expiration dates are confusing — and not just because they don’t necessarily indicate when you should throw food out. “Sell by” and “best by” refer to peak quality, not safety. And to add to the confusion, the terms aren’t federally regulated or required (except in the case of baby formula and certain baby foods). Most foods are fine after the dates on their packaging pass, though they may be slightly subpar. There are a handful of foods, however, where timing actually does matter. In these cases, it’s less about flavor and more about whether that meal is going to haunt you tomorrow. Here are the foods you should toss once the expiration date has passed (or sooner if you’ve opened them). | | | | |

Peter,**It’s a new era in Texas**. Tired of higher costs and Trump’s corruption, Texans voted for change and knocked out MAGA candidates up and down the ballot. Flipping our state was _**years**_ in the making. # [](https://act.betoorourke.com/go/43706?t=1&akid=241179%2E444211%2ErQ8wvX)
Last year, Ken Paxton launched a baseless investigation into Powered by People and dragged us to court to try to bankrupt us and shut us down.
We had to spend over _$600,000 on legal fees,_ but we stood our ground. We won and got right back to work registering voters and staying in touch with them to make sure they turn out.
**On Election Day, we beat him again. Texans sent James Talarico to the Senate instead of Paxton, and years of our organizing helped make the difference in close races all over the state.**
Paxton came after us because he knows our organizing works. When we show up for a young person on a college campus or a family in a small town, they show up for us at the polls.
The numbers prove it: **68.17% of voters in our network cast a ballot in the midterms. That’s 16 points above the statewide turnout rate.**
We’re not wasting any time. We’re already back on the road, hitting college campuses, to keep organizing in every corner of Texas no matter what people like Ken Paxton throw our way.

On Monday, the Senate voted 73-25 to advance the _Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act_. That’s a big step forward, and I’m grateful for your support. Now comes the hard part. [**The bill heads into the amendment process before a final vote, and I need you with me.**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/143416917/660138005/1356710392?refcode=AU_MTH_EG_GEN_PET_AC_20261113_PM1_V1_S1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDYvMS84OTA0NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI4MGU3ZjU3Ny1hOWRmLWYxMTEtOTFmMC0wMDBkM2ExOGUyNDQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=lnkqI7ySFscfnrSg5qM292KkfOvLgRq3XQ2bzBMx9C0=&emci=7ee7f577-a9df-f111-91f0-000d3a18e244&emdi=80e7f577-a9df-f111-91f0-000d3a18e244&ceid=252045) This is the bipartisan permitting deal I’ve been telling you about. It delivers for families like yours:
* Lowers energy costs: an estimated $19 billion in savings on home electricity bills
* Creates up to 105,600 good-paying trades and manufacturing jobs by 2040
* Makes new data centers pay an additional $35 billion for the grid and energy costs they create, instead of sticking families with the bill
* Nearly doubles the solar and wind that can connect to the grid

And it does all of this while protecting and creating key environmental and consultation safeguards, protecting the public’s ability to challenge projects, and securing dedicated funding to clean up abandoned hardrock mines. The AFL-CIO, LiUNA, IBEW, and the nation’s largest building trades unions have endorsed it, along with clean energy producers, manufacturing groups, and state and local officials. As Chair of the Rules Committee, Virginia Foxx directly blocked the House from voting on Trump’s tariffs and the release of the Epstein files. When Elon Musk and DOGE ransacked our federal government last year, she stood by and cheered them on. She’s made a name for herself yelling at reporters to shut up and screaming at staff for using the wrong elevator. And for twenty years, she’s stepped on the backs of working people in order to climb the ladder in Washington, DC, all while making millions playing the stock market. Dear Friend, One week after a hard election night, the state Freedom Caucuses aren't spending their time looking backward. In **Missouri** , our members were elected to the top floor jobs in both chambers and **Montana** House Republicans chose Freedom Caucus Member Tom Millett as their new Majority Leader. In **Illinois** and **Montana** , caucus members started holding the winners to the promises they made on the campaign trail. Here's what your support made possible this week.
---
|
---
**MISSOURI FREEDOM CAUCUS TAKES THE LEAD IN BOTH CHAMBERS**
---
[Last Thursday, MOFC Chairman Sen. Nick Schroer was elected Senate Majority Leader, and MOFC member Rep. Darin Chappell was elected House Majority Leader for the coming session](http://give.statefreedomcaucus.org/ls/click?upn=u001.SSCAglCEkhp55PDWKhWTjlGtTaWglf8SUGjOni7plj2BNjfoiblroI5-2Ban4ecSMHN2JmbjbOX79XYkdk9R5lctEurH0yWJ1OvKjt-2FkR-2F-2B0w-3DwTf0_9XnTPLnaEjN9OHWhKYUffDeECIVzR9M-2B5LaO5RH8NVBZyx1SQGGYhOdwcjZYtHerAJBUHq9-2BVcwi3MOGCBORUOiFLRtBjWPf1dUxs4MQohT07FPYTw4CPXP1s9XDhIM-2BQlzyayuA1TxufNBfIJNNBzwQQLgKnU7XuGsxKwmfRphe74jqNFdHRCF5kW06oxBOsbAaqmRxt1D5dfKUIz07nelRtFaxTmTkn6kA6GdzXF-2F9Z4NlibdZaMGYB1I7EfjFzJaPGnX4NPPZWD5qsP2tWNsmyJqmEoBMEF7zpzNNcaw-3D). That puts Freedom Caucus members in position to help set the agenda and guide the work of both chambers of the Missouri General Assembly. MOFC didn't treat it as a victory lap. In its statement, the caucus said the message from voters was unmistakable: Missourians are tired of empty promises, and the time to deliver is now. MOFC laid out the work ahead: real tax relief for working families, seniors, veterans, and small businesses; putting students first and giving parents a stronger voice; lowering health care costs with more transparency; rooting out fraud and waste; and making Missouri a place families can afford.

[The same momentum reached Washington. Jim Jordan, a founder and former chairman of the House Freedom Caucus, was elected House Republican Leader, and the Network called it a great win for the Freedom Caucus movement](http://give.statefreedomcaucus.org/ls/click?upn=u001.SSCAglCEkhp55PDWKhWTjnkL6r5HK0BBEZCfRCSbNiS0cB3NtIOa-2Br2Bm6OEiY43ACXJbXamBpf-2BNuJdtj2ziA-3D-3DMQBK_9XnTPLnaEjN9OHWhKYUffDeECIVzR9M-2B5LaO5RH8NVBZyx1SQGGYhOdwcjZYtHerAJBUHq9-2BVcwi3MOGCBORUOiFLRtBjWPf1dUxs4MQohT07FPYTw4CPXP1s9XDhIM-2BQlzyayuA1TxufNBfIJNNBzwQQLgKnU7XuGsxKwmfRphyvHXs5lpQE-2FEUbK9TM2pdk3qfvVCQ0g-2FfRaPPxTVFZj8V7QUrTSbmBYMnkNTU6HAF2uy7f4ba0XPgE0FBO46yht8hU34Vf1btFFNd8cjvIXS26hijMFLzDXGwK6mNSuw-3D). **Why it matters: when Freedom Caucus members are the ones running the floor, the conservative agenda stops being a wish list and becomes a schedule.**

**CAMPAIGN SEASON IS OVER. NOW KEEP THE PROMISES.**
---
The **Illinois Freedom Caucus** is putting the majority party on notice. Ahead of the veto session, ILFC is pressing Gov. Pritzker and legislative leaders to pass the Family Farm Preservation Act, HB4736, which would raise the estate tax threshold and adjust it for inflation. The caucus pointed out that the Illinois Farm Bureau has made this reform a priority for several sessions, the votes are there, and Pritzker said he supported it during his 2026 campaign. ILFC's message is simple: preserve family farms, right now.
