In Montana, the **Montana Freedom Caucus** is making sure voters know what to watch when the 2027 session opens. [The caucus is reminding Montanans that in 2025, a bloc of Republicans it calls the "Nasty Nine" in the Senate and the "Dirty Dozen" in the House teamed up with Democrats to form a new majority and pass a Democrat agenda.](http://give.statefreedomcaucus.org/ls/click?upn=u001.SSCAglCEkhp55PDWKhWTjmuAKmNlhopAWiF8Etm8k1DPY-2BW3Z97bKuNm5If0oGribxdfNCxbLL9S0p4iHJTLAOBHEz2uqCDtgPlhX9a-2F9SU-3D2LcX_9XnTPLnaEjN9OHWhKYUffDeECIVzR9M-2B5LaO5RH8NVBZyx1SQGGYhOdwcjZYtHerAJBUHq9-2BVcwi3MOGCBORUOiFLRtBjWPf1dUxs4MQohT07FPYTw4CPXP1s9XDhIM-2BQlzyayuA1TxufNBfIJNNBzwQQLgKnU7XuGsxKwmfRpjubwdIC4-2B2B-2BbMw-2BKF22qHJnajjpU2Ki35wHf1pa63UZsm-2FOMotrhHoWUAFd7p3pp3fRVKaaBNCN-2BODvUSGmdI8i1ARBxLdrU5LgkdDRatietsi7UR209k6FzjEihpCLs-3D) MTFC is asking whether that bloc will push higher taxes, higher fees, or more spending next session, and it's urging supporters to watch the bills and the votes themselves at [legmt.gov.](http://give.statefreedomcaucus.org/ls/click?upn=u001.SSCAglCEkhp55PDWKhWTjoBWA0vk6jD3upTbuqDPdpw-3DqCpI_9XnTPLnaEjN9OHWhKYUffDeECIVzR9M-2B5LaO5RH8NVBZyx1SQGGYhOdwcjZYtHerAJBUHq9-2BVcwi3MOGCBORUOiFLRtBjWPf1dUxs4MQohT07FPYTw4CPXP1s9XDhIM-2BQlzyayuA1TxufNBfIJNNBzwQQLgKnU7XuGsxKwmfRpjeQSAWlcrRI1ErQBvS27MNecL2Lv4tN9OpuMdIl0HtDI363qe8si6fuvYPtsgbDnOP936-2BX4TZqoUrkoABRMbpGu-2BaDZI5wgfZPQTgEWJczLuW5eWp0Mg30BxUbjah8ns-3D) The caucus is already putting those questions to the state's proposed 2029 biennium budget. In a new graphic, MTFC laid out seven hard questions, including why Montana would keep taxing Social Security benefits and military retirement pay, where the lasting fix for property taxes is, why spending shouldn't be frozen after HB 2 grew 18 percent last cycle, and whether government education is helping Montana's children succeed. The caucus also asked why the proposal returns just $220 million to taxpayers, where the prior multibillion-dollar balance went, why another $300 million would be added to reserves, and why there are so many one-time-only funding requests that add up to $618 million. MTFC's closing point: last session's legislation was signed and sold as covering these expenses, so why does this budget ask for more one-time-only funding?

⚡️ **Texas** : [Network Joins Call for a Special Session](http://give.statefreedomcaucus.org/ls/click?upn=u001.SSCAglCEkhp55PDWKhWTjnkL6r5HK0BBEZCfRCSbNiTpcjylK5zz4xlHSOoJ-2FaHPWSezbirH1RzVsHRzXYEcQQ-3D-3DPAAK_9XnTPLnaEjN9OHWhKYUffDeECIVzR9M-2B5LaO5RH8NVBZyx1SQGGYhOdwcjZYtHerAJBUHq9-2BVcwi3MOGCBORUOiFLRtBjWPf1dUxs4MQohT07FPYTw4CPXP1s9XDhIM-2BQlzyayuA1TxufNBfIJNNBzwQQLgKnU7XuGsxKwmfRpiNEL0KGFQDQMHelIScN6rjxFrEbOInqGc2LtD1418o6BjjsbIlPNqcx4BtPZ2ZWWztXpkQA8EEMirFnmQ1KsiJt7DOtnMmjz6-2BWITGbDXSjta90oJOMADhNFEkXMkh7y8-3D). The State Freedom Caucus Network joined a long list of conservative groups calling on Gov. Greg Abbott to convene a special session to rein in the governor's emergency powers before Democrats take control. "No governor should have unchecked authority to both make and enforce laws," the Network said, thanking Citizens for Renewing America for leading the charge. The coalition letter, signed by the Network and groups including Texas Eagle Forum, Gun Owners of America, the American Principles Project, and the Election Integrity Network, asks Abbott to call the Legislature back immediately to put meaningful limits on those powers. Among the reforms the letter seeks: prohibit the governor from suspending or modifying statutes, sunset emergency orders in 30 days unless the legislature ratifies them, bar the reissuing of expired or rejected orders, require emergency orders to be narrowly tailored, and subject them to expedited judicial review. ⚡️ **Wyoming** : [WYFC Calls Out Cheyenne's Priorities](http://give.statefreedomcaucus.org/ls/click?upn=u001.SSCAglCEkhp55PDWKhWTjppHen015Gx6AaFY6rk-2BtVkcPs-2B-2F-2FbEUFYlU3kG89SJd8z-2FvS0w2Fo-2BB8Gsl7GoOscAdlwOTIK0h61WVE2DhTrU-3DUvfP_9XnTPLnaEjN9OHWhKYUffDeECIVzR9M-2B5LaO5RH8NVBZyx1SQGGYhOdwcjZYtHerAJBUHq9-2BVcwi3MOGCBORUOiFLRtBjWPf1dUxs4MQohT07FPYTw4CPXP1s9XDhIM-2BQlzyayuA1TxufNBfIJNNBzwQQLgKnU7XuGsxKwmfRphq27cXEGBKJLWdiiCmP8n52IF42h9z3Bc-2F3S-2FfXd7-2BdcNImnsSXgt5fk3fPU9GRwcKuT-2FZtTcEa52cRtokoxE7ISjxBFq2ZAHAK-2Bej6hfDUUuBYEg7-2FKqZz0m3MNoo7ZU-3D). The Wyoming Freedom Caucus is exposing a double standard at Cheyenne City Hall. WYFC says city leaders are rolling out the red carpet for multibillion-dollar big tech data centers while forcibly annexing a beloved family-run urban farm. So much for being "open for business." The caucus is pointing supporters to a real fix: the Legislature's Joint Corporations Committee is hearing a bill that would allow recall elections of local officials, giving residents a way to hold city leaders accountable between elections. The hearing is in Cheyenne on December 10 and 11, and WYFC wants Wyomingites there to make their voices heard. ⚡️ **Maryland** : [MDFC Holds Moore to His Own Words](http://give.statefreedomcaucus.org/ls/click?upn=u001.SSCAglCEkhp55PDWKhWTjiwkZmtXDP4u12gaI7rwUjbWcO4aNkxfRRFAXh8s1zvnMDvmeOFpcPi1QDokkEuDdxeE6g336LwDGSrhHKFOTrQ-3Doy9L_9XnTPLnaEjN9OHWhKYUffDeECIVzR9M-2B5LaO5RH8NVBZyx1SQGGYhOdwcjZYtHerAJBUHq9-2BVcwi3MOGCBORUOiFLRtBjWPf1dUxs4MQohT07FPYTw4CPXP1s9XDhIM-2BQlzyayuA1TxufNBfIJNNBzwQQLgKnU7XuGsxKwmfRpha2UJmkUqHOZAOXWPZGrZHYM0BfrtOuD9acSsbB8eZX7fOKgFTi5zAB6VbF-2FewdrTdBgGZf8f9vJ9H2lgzWaXIy3tzaELlhuacYzx9w6uzGwvfJcUH8D-2FG61nwh6PFoEE-3D). The Maryland Freedom Caucus spent the fall warning voters about the push to redraw Maryland's congressional map. One week after what MDFC calls the theft of the last congressional seat held by Maryland's Republican voters, the caucus is pointing out the contrast: Gov. Wes Moore is now promoting a book about healing divisions, which MDFC sees as the launch of a presidential campaign. Why it matters: Marylanders deserve leaders whose actions match their words, and MDFC will keep putting the two side by side so voters can judge for themselves.

clean_body: | | | | | Dear Friend, One week after a hard election night, the state Freedom Caucuses aren't spending their time looking backward. In Missouri , our members were elected to the top floor jobs in both chambers and Montana House Republicans chose Freedom Caucus Member Tom Millett as their new Majority Leader. In Illinois and Montana , caucus members started holding the winners to the promises they made on the campaign trail. Here's what your support made possible this week. | MISSOURI FREEDOM CAUCUS TAKES THE LEAD IN BOTH CHAMBERS . That puts Freedom Caucus members in position to help set the agenda and guide the work of both chambers of the Missouri General Assembly. MOFC didn't treat it as a victory lap. In its statement, the caucus said the message from voters was unmistakable: Missourians are tired of empty promises, and the time to deliver is now. MOFC laid out the work ahead: real tax relief for working families, seniors, veterans, and small businesses; putting students first and giving parents a stronger voice; lowering health care costs with more transparency; rooting out fraud and waste; and making Missouri a place families can afford. . Why it matters: when Freedom Caucus members are the ones running the floor, the conservative agenda stops being a wish list and becomes a schedule. | CAMPAIGN SEASON IS OVER. NOW KEEP THE PROMISES. The Illinois Freedom Caucus is putting the majority party on notice. Ahead of the veto session, ILFC is pressing Gov. Pritzker and legislative leaders to pass the Family Farm Preservation Act, HB4736, which would raise the estate tax threshold and adjust it for inflation. The caucus pointed out that the Illinois Farm Bureau has made this reform a priority for several sessions, the votes are there, and Pritzker said he supported it during his 2026 campaign. ILFC's message is simple: preserve family farms, right now. In Montana, the Montana Freedom Caucus is making sure voters know what to watch when the 2027 session opens. MTFC is asking whether that bloc will push higher taxes, higher fees, or more spending next session, and it's urging supporters to watch the bills and the votes themselves at The caucus is already putting those questions to the state's proposed 2029 biennium budget. In a new graphic, MTFC laid out seven hard questions, including why Montana would keep taxing Social Security benefits and military retirement pay, where the lasting fix for property taxes is, why spending shouldn't be frozen after HB 2 grew 18 percent last cycle, and whether government education is helping Montana's children succeed. The caucus also asked why the proposal returns just $220 million to taxpayers, where the prior multibillion-dollar balance went, why another $300 million would be added to reserves, and why there are so many one-time-only funding requests that add up to $618 million. MTFC's closing point: last session's legislation was signed and sold as covering these expenses, so why does this budget ask for more one-time-only funding? Why it matters: promises on the campaign trail cost nothing. A caucus that tracks the votes and asks for them in public is what turns those promises into law, and that's exactly the work your support makes possible. | PODCAST CLIP OF THE WEEK State Freedom Caucus Unfiltered this week features South Dakota state Rep. Heather Baxter, a South Dakota Freedom Caucus member who just won her race for secretary of state. The clip walks through how Baxter kept pushing election integrity bills, and how lobbyists and the secretary of state's office showed up to oppose them. So she ran for secretary of state herself, and she won. As Unfiltered put it, "Problem solved." | QUICK HITS ⚡️ Texas : . The State Freedom Caucus Network joined a long list of conservative groups calling on Gov. Greg Abbott to convene a special session to rein in the governor's emergency powers before Democrats take control. "No governor should have unchecked authority to both make and enforce laws," the Network said, thanking Citizens for Renewing America for leading the charge. The coalition letter, signed by the Network and groups including Texas Eagle Forum, Gun Owners of America, the American Principles Project, and the Election Integrity Network, asks Abbott to call the Legislature back immediately to put meaningful limits on those powers. Among the reforms the letter seeks: prohibit the governor from suspending or modifying statutes, sunset emergency orders in 30 days unless the legislature ratifies them, bar the reissuing of expired or rejected orders, require emergency orders to be narrowly tailored, and subject them to expedited judicial review. ⚡️ Wyoming : . The Wyoming Freedom Caucus is exposing a double standard at Cheyenne City Hall. WYFC says city leaders are rolling out the red carpet for multibillion-dollar big tech data centers while forcibly annexing a beloved family-run urban farm. So much for being "open for business." The caucus is pointing supporters to a real fix: the Legislature's Joint Corporations Committee is hearing a bill that would allow recall elections of local officials, giving residents a way to hold city leaders accountable between elections. The hearing is in Cheyenne on December 10 and 11, and WYFC wants Wyomingites there to make their voices heard. ⚡️ Maryland : . The Maryland Freedom Caucus spent the fall warning voters about the push to redraw Maryland's congressional map. One week after what MDFC calls the theft of the last congressional seat held by Maryland's Republican voters, the caucus is pointing out the contrast: Gov. Wes Moore is now promoting a book about healing divisions, which MDFC sees as the launch of a presidential campaign. Why it matters: Marylanders deserve leaders whose actions match their words, and MDFC will keep putting the two side by side so voters can judge for themselves. | HELP US KEEP BUILDING Every leadership win, every bill pushed, and every vote brought into the light starts with supporters like you. Help us keep building. We'll be back with another update soon. Until then, please be sure to our efforts so that we can support our State Freedom Caucuses!In Liberty, Andy RothPresidentState Freedom Caucus Network | |

The Democrats who won on November 3 will tell you they won on affordability, but affordability doesn't sell out a 250-seat theater in Minneapolis in five minutes. Hasan Piker does.
[A week before the election](https://substack.com/redirect/6da86ac6-9709-4d32-b76c-7b817655c7fb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), Piker sat on stage next to Rep. Ilhan Omar at the University of Minnesota, and organizers said openly that they brought him in to turn out voters under 40. He did the same for Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan, for Zohran Mamdani in New York, and for a [slate of candidates](https://substack.com/redirect/d69359ff-c139-47fd-8bff-5665ea49850a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) from California to Tennessee. The socially acceptable explanation for the Democrat sweep is frustration with the Iran war. The real one is that the party handed its youth turnout operation to a man who wants the United States to lose and sides with the Islamic terrorists working to make that happen on the battlefield and within the homeland.
Although born in New Jersey, he was raised in Istanbul, is ethnically Turkish, and has shown far more loyalty to his Islamic heritage than to the United States. He started his career on his uncle Cenk Uygur's Young Turks, a program named after the [group guilty of the Armenian Genocide](https://substack.com/redirect/9942aa24-9f29-4ded-af37-6b7d19548ecf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), which murdered more than one million Christians.

● Threatening to put [Republicans in jail](https://substack.com/redirect/647a56c5-94a7-4380-94ed-44d23b31af2e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), including [the President](https://substack.com/redirect/3ba800a2-ae7a-41fe-a698-4b05004adc7f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).

body:
Families are tired of a government that spends more time fighting than fixing

| |
---
Friend, In January, Democrats will take back the majority in the House of Representatives, and Nellie will be part of it. A lot of the conversation since Election Day has focused on accountability. For the past two years, there's been almost no check on this administration from the House. A Democratic majority means real oversight and real answers for the American people. But voters in North Jersey didn't send Nellie back to Congress just to hold hearings. They sent her back because gas, groceries, and rent still cost too much, and because families are tired of a government that spends more time fighting than fixing. That's what Nellie heard from residents, and it's what she's going back to Washington to work on. body:

Peter --
Here’s the truth: We’re running on empty.
While we are still waiting for every vote to be counted, we are starting to run out of resources.
I am so grateful to have had your support throughout this campaign. Seriously.
We started with $0 in our bank account, and we built this movement from the ground up without a dime from the greedy corporations hurting all of us. And we spent almost everything we had to win -- _and we will._
So we need your help again to keep us afloat while we fight to count every vote and power through until this race is certified. We can’t afford to fall short when Donald Trump and the entire DC establishment are working to overturn the results of our election and undo the will of Alaskans if I win.
I am so proud that this campaign is fueled by working people. But that does mean we have to keep asking for your support until this race is officially over.
I wouldn’t ask if it wasn’t so important. So please Peter:
**[Will you please split a donation between my campaign and Wes Moore to help make sure every vote is protected and counted fairly, and support all of our work through the finish line? name: Representative Ryan Chamberlin
subject: Honoring our veterans, supporting our community
body:
Veterans Day in Belleview, a new fire station in Ocala, and the work ahead on property taxes.

Ryan Chamberlin for State Representative

https://clicks.aweber.com/y/ct/?l=1fqto&m=f.KNkz.GmM5liyD&b=Ug2HWvf.xfmVLoiLrk8VwQ

DISTRICT 24 NEWSLETTER

NOVEMBER 12, 2026

FROM RYAN’S DESK

A week of gratitude and service.
Friends and Neighbors,
This week, I had the honor of joining Belleview Christian Academy for its Veterans Service and speaking with the next generation about what it means to be free. To every veteran in our community, thank you for your courage, your sacrifice and your commitment to our country.

I also attended the opening of Ocala Fire Station 8 and the Give4Marion check presentation. I’m grateful for the firefighters, nonprofit leaders, volunteers and donors who keep showing up for our neighbors.
Those visits are part of what I want to bring back to Tallahassee. Families deserve to feel safe, to be heard and to have confidence that their tax dollars are being spent responsibly. I’ll keep pushing for that accountability as we continue the work on property taxes.
Below are a few moments from the week and an update on what Amendment 3 means moving forward.
God bless,
Ryan Chamberlin

NOVEMBER 11 · BELLEVIEW

Honoring our veterans
Ryan speaking at Belleview Christian Academy’s Veterans Service

https://clicks.aweber.com/y/ct/?l=1fqto&m=f.KNkz.GmM5liyD&b=.Ck14a8AixAWwl2Z89QCbw

I was grateful to attend Belleview Christian Academy’s Veterans Service and talk with students about the freedom we enjoy as Americans. Thank you to the school for bringing generations together to honor those who served. To our veterans and their families, we appreciate you.
See the Veterans Day photos →

https://clicks.aweber.com/y/ct/?l=1fqto&m=f.KNkz.GmM5liyD&b=.Ck14a8AixAWwl2Z89QCbw

NOVEMBER 9 · OCALA

Welcoming Fire Station 8
Ryan outside Ocala Fire Station 8 with a fire engine

https://clicks.aweber.com/y/ct/?l=1fqto&m=f.KNkz.GmM5liyD&b=XYgfyJiWQJx3eUI3D5cCJA
I joined Ocala Fire Rescue for the grand opening of Fire Station 8. Thank you to the men and women who serve our community and to everyone who helped make this new station possible. Our firefighters deserve the facilities and resources they need to do their jobs.

See the station opening →

https://clicks.aweber.com/y/ct/?l=1fqto&m=f.KNkz.GmM5liyD&b=XYgfyJiWQJx3eUI3D5cCJA

NOVEMBER 10 · MARION COUNTY

Celebrating the people who give back
Ryan speaking at the Give4Marion check presentation

https://clicks.aweber.com/y/ct/?l=1fqto&m=f.KNkz.GmM5liyD&b=xwoquKx1cMQqksu_Ofv9Xg

On Tuesday, I attended the Give4Marion check presentation celebrating our local nonprofits. This year’s campaign raised more than $2.3 million from 4,618 donors. Thank you to everyone who gave, volunteered, sponsored or helped spread the word. Your generosity supports organizations serving neighbors throughout Marion County.
See the Give4Marion update →

https://clicks.aweber.com/y/ct/?l=1fqto&m=f.KNkz.GmM5liyD&b=xwoquKx1cMQqksu_Ofv9Xg

PROPERTY TAX UPDATE

What changes next year

Florida voters approved Amendment 3, and the Department of Revenue says it first applies to the 2027 tax roll. Your November 2026 bill is unaffected.
For eligible homesteads, the non-school exemption rises to $150,000 in 2027 and $250,000 in 2028, with inflation adjustments afterward. The amendment also lowers the annual assessment-growth cap for non-homestead property from 10% to 5%. It leaves the school-tax exemption unchanged. Eligibility timing differs for people who are not Florida residents by December 31, 2026.

I supported that relief, and I’ll keep working toward eliminating and replacing the property-tax system. My priorities include reviewing local spending, protecting essential services and developing a fair replacement for the revenue. Those next steps still require work in Tallahassee.
Read the state’s explanation →

https://clicks.aweber.com/y/ct/?l=1fqto&m=f.KNkz.GmM5liyD&b=7P620yICZH86rDKYHGjDyw

A PERSONAL NOTE

Happy birthday, Jenny
Ryan and Jenny in the photo shared with her birthday message

https://clicks.aweber.com/y/ct/?l=1fqto&m=f.KNkz.GmM5liyD&b=hNf3OiqQ93QgoaLbAb0r1A
Last week, we celebrated Jenny’s birthday. I’m grateful for the wife and mother she is and for everything she means to our family. Happy birthday, Jenny. We love you.

Keep the conversation going
The Property Tax Truth Tour continues as we discuss what comes next. If your church, civic group or neighborhood organization would like to host a conversation, connect with the team.

Your generosity supports organizations serving neighbors throughout Marion County. Your November 2026 bill is unaffected. For eligible homesteads, the non-school exemption rises to $150,000 in 2027 and $250,000 in 2028, with inflation adjustments afterward. The amendment also lowers the annual assessment-growth cap for non-homestead property from 10% to 5%. It leaves the school-tax exemption unchanged. Eligibility timing differs for people who are not Florida residents by December 31, 2026. I supported that relief, and I’ll keep working toward eliminating and replacing the property-tax system. My priorities include reviewing local spending, protecting essential services and developing a fair replacement for the revenue. Those next steps still require work in Tallahassee. Dear Collective Community,
Thank you! This cycle, you gave, shared our slate with your networks, and stood with Black candidates in every corner of the country. On November 3rd, that work paid off.
In 2026, The Collective PAC made 192 endorsements, our second-largest slate in ten years. Our active slate of 146 Black leaders, in 35 states, the District of Columbia and the U.S. Virgin Islands, ran for every level on the ballot, from the U.S. Senate to the county courthouse.
More than half of our endorsed candidates on the general election ballot ran below the statewide level. Many were first-time candidates without big donor networks, which is exactly where your support goes the furthest.
So far this season, 108 of our endorsed candidates have won their seats: 100 out of 121 races on November 3rd and eight earlier in the year, an 83% win rate. Across the full cycle, 56% of our endorsed races ended in a win, compared with 50% from 2016 through 2025. Five races are still too close to call, and we are confirming results in 12 more.
* * *
# **History was made up and down the ballot:**
* **Scott Colom (MS) won Mississippi 's U.S. Senate race**, unseating Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith. He is the first Black U.S. senator from Mississippi since Blanche K. Bruce left office in 1881.
* **Two Black women were elected governor on the same night.** **Keisha Lance Bottoms (GA)** became Georgia's first Black governor and the first Black woman ever elected governor of a U.S. state. **Stacey Plaskett (VI)** became the first woman elected Governor of the U.S. Virgin Islands.
* **Aaron Ford (NV)** and **David Crowley (WI)** were elected the first Black governors of Nevada and Wisconsin, and **Wes Moore (MD)** won re-election in Maryland.
* **Juliana Stratton (IL)** was elected to the U.S. Senate, the second Black woman Illinois has sent to the Senate, after Carol Moseley Braun. **Cory Booker (NJ)** won re-election.
* **Tanya Miller (GA)** became the first woman elected Attorney General of Georgia. All six of our attorney general candidates and all four of our lieutenant governor candidates won.
* Nine of our candidates are headed to Congress for the first time:
* **Melat Kiros (CO-01)**
* **Jasmine Clark (GA-13)**
* **Donna Miller (IL-02)**
* **La Shawn Ford (IL-07)**
* **Adrian Boafo (MD-05)**
* **Raymond Smith, Jr. (NC-03)** - flipped Republican held seat
* **LaKesha Womack (NC-14)** - flipped Republican held seat
* **Chris Rabb (PA-03)**
* **Frederick D. Haynes III (TX-30)**.
* Our candidates also flipped vital state legislative seats: **Theresa Brooks (MI)** won Michigan Senate District 9, **Chaunt e Gilmore (OK)** won Oklahoma House District 100, and **Paula Swift (CA)** won California Assembly District 70, each unseating a Republican incumbent.

We also honor the candidates whose races did not go our way, including **Angie Nixon (FL), Charles Booker (KY), Jamie Davis (LA) and N 'Kiyla Jasmine Thomas (OK) for U.S. Senate; Jermaine Johnson (SC) for governor, Annette Blackwell (OH) for state auditor, and Karen Bass (CA) for Mayor of Los Angeles**. They ran with courage and built real power in their communities, and we are proud to have stood with them.
**[Click here to view the election results for our 2026 endorsed candidates.](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/5dd666d8-3396-4ddd-b010-fb1881d7e131?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
* * *
# **Action Items:**
**Join our National Finance Council.** The National Finance Council is The Collective PAC's national network of donors who raise money for our candidates and voter engagement work. Members are invited to candidate fundraisers, like this fall's Michigan Power Hour in Detroit, and get updates on our candidates throughout the cycle. To help fund the 2027-2028 bench, join at **[collectivepac.org/nfc](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/0e5cef28-793b-4c97-b407-fcf3d72227c1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**.
**Build the 2027 -2028 bench with us.** Recruitment for the 2027 and 2028 cycles begins this December. If your organization knows Black leaders who are ready to run, email **[political@collectivepac.org](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/c1531f0b-b4da-4552-ab9b-465709e11741?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**.
**Subscribe to our Substack.** We post news about our candidates and our work there throughout the year. Subscribe at **[collectivepac.substack.com](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/86324671-d0b6-4b46-a324-6e2be3358e90?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** and share it with your network.
**Help us build Black political power.** Our work doesn't end on Election Day. To help us keep this momentum going, we must continue investing in Black leadership and preparing the next generation of Black candidates to run and win. **[Will you pitch in $15 to support us, so we can continue investing in Black leadership and pave the way for more historic victories?](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/05a04361-5c50-4d29-9f92-d9e62dfc3197?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[ DONATE >>](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/05a04361-5c50-4d29-9f92-d9e62dfc3197?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
As we often say, "To change the laws, we must change the lawmakers." This season, 108 new and returning Black leaders earned the chance to do exactly that. We are grateful for your partnership as we continue to Build Black Political Power.
With gratitude,
_Quentin James & Stefanie Brown James_
_Co-Founders_
_The Collective PAC_

* * *
_We fought four years to win in 2024. Republicans had two years to deliver. What the hell happened?_
I am spitting nails.
For four years after 2020, Americans paid a price for their political convictions. Families fractured. Friendships ended. Careers and reputations were destroyed. People faced prosecution, imprisonment, financial ruin, and public humiliation. January 6 defendants and their families endured years of legal battles, separation, and financial hardship. Some defendants died by suicide. Whatever anyone thinks about January 6, those families suffered consequences no election victory could erase.
We organized, volunteered, donated, knocked on doors, defended our convictions, and showed up at the polls. By 2024 we were exhausted, but we weren't about to quit. We were told to make the election **too big to rig** , and we did everything within our power to deliver.
We weren't expecting miracles. We knew the mess was enormous and that Washington would fight every inch. What I never imagined was that two years later I would still be wondering whether the Republicans we elected had the slightest appreciation for what it took to put them in office.
**Four years of absolute hell to win in 2024, and Republicans managed to squander the opportunity in two.**
How the hell did we get here?
I was a registered Independent until Donald Trump came along. I've never had much use for career politicians who promise to fix problems, become part of the problem, and then run again on the same promises. In the private sector that record gets you fired. In Washington it gets you a leadership post and a standing ovation.
**These people couldn 't run a lemonade stand, but they think they're qualified to run the country.**
Trump appealed because he wasn't one of them. He was a builder and a negotiator. I never bought the claim that he is stupid. You don't build that kind of business record by being the bumbling idiot his critics need him to be.
I've said it many times: **Trump is playing world-class chess while the left is playing checkers.**
Which makes the 2026 midterms all the more maddening.

If Trump is playing world-class chess, how in God's name did Republicans lose the board?
I didn't expect him to personally manage Congress. I did expect him to recognize the people who couldn't execute, deal with them, and make certain his administration wasn't wasting the opportunity Americans fought four years to give him.
Trump knows better than anyone that a brilliant strategy is worthless if the people responsible for executing it can't deliver.
So I have questions for him, too. When did he recognize that congressional leadership wasn't getting the job done? What did he do about it? And why did Republicans reach November with priorities still unfinished?
I have defended Trump's intelligence for years. I'm not about to insult it now by pretending he bears no responsibility for the people and decisions surrounding his administration.
**If you 're playing world-class chess, you had better know who's moving your pieces.**
**What Exactly Did Republicans Do With the Opportunity We Gave Them?**
I spent years on business turnarounds. When a company is in trouble you don't get paid for explaining why the deal didn't close. You get paid to close it. Republicans knew the Senate rules, the margins, the opposition, and the date of the next election. None of this was a surprise.
So why did so much remain unfinished? Explain what the plan was to overcome the obstacles. Explain what was tried, what failed, and why the strategy wasn't changed when time started running out.
After everything Trump and his supporters went through with the old establishment, Senate Republicans chose John Thune--a longtime member of Mitch McConnell's leadership orbit--over Rick Scott. Scott was eliminated in the first round. After the 2026 losses they reelected Thune unopposed.
* * *
# **We 're not giving up this fight, and neither should you**
The midterms were a wake up call to all American patriots...
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/9f6cffaf-68d3-49f8-abef-e8241a1f365d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The battle ahead will surely be hard and up-hill. But think of the brave Americans who stormed the beaches of Normandy, or the men who fought and bled at Shiloh and Lexington.
They had a dream for America they were willing to die for. We cannot let their sacrifice be in vain.
This is what we believe in.
We must fight for our nation with everything we've got, even on the darkest days, as our ancestors did.
### **PolitiBrawl will hold our place in line on the battleground for information and news.**
We appreciate your readership and support.

Do not give up hope. Tomorrow is a brighter day.
* * *
_**(Piece continues):**_
### **You cannot make this stuff up.**
Speaker Mike Johnson has said nearly 700 House-passed measures were awaiting Senate action. Not every bill is a priority, but the backlog raises the obvious question about what Senate leadership was doing with the limited time it had.
On nominations, as of November 12 there were still 195 civilian nominations awaiting Senate action, 157 of which had not cleared committee. The Senate confirmed hundreds and changed some procedures to speed things up. An administration still needs its people in place. That isn't complicated.
In what other profession does management preside over a disaster and get rewarded with another term? Only in Washington.
**Six Years of Election-Integrity Concerns. And We Still Didn 't Get It Done.**
This one absolutely infuriates me.
Americans have been arguing about voter rolls, identification, citizenship verification, and election administration since 2020. Six years of controversy and declining confidence among a large share of the electorate.
The House passed the SAVE Act in April 2025 and the SAVE America Act in February 2026. Neither became law before the midterms. Republicans knew the opposition and the Senate's rules. If the votes weren't there, what alternatives were considered? If leadership concluded it couldn't pass, why wasn't that explained to the people who had been told for years that this was essential?
I am not interested in another fundraising email about election integrity. I want the explanation for why Republicans entered the 2026 midterms without it. And now, with Democrats taking control of Congress, how exactly do they propose to get it done?
**Enough With the Damn Parties and Air Force One Selfies.**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/9f6cffaf-68d3-49f8-abef-e8241a1f365d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
[ Upgrade to paid](https://substack..WsXNpHSjGicDN1RHu8nlqWvVmYO6U69Y_iUlmfNme_U?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=224793144)
To the people inside the Trump White House: **read the damn room.**
I open social media and there it is again. Another fabulous reception. Another glamorous dinner. Another Air Force One selfie. Another VIP experience accompanied by a breathless post about what an extraordinary privilege it is to be there.
We get it. You're having the time of your lives.
Americans are standing at gas pumps, paying outrageous insurance premiums, and trying to figure out how their grocery bills got so high. Republicans just suffered a political disaster. Election-integrity legislation never made it across the finish line.
And the White House social scene appears to be thriving.
**What exactly are we celebrating?**
I understand the excitement of working in the White House. But the relentless boasting is becoming revolting when the priorities Americans were told were urgent remain unfinished.
If Republicans had delivered on their promises, starting with securing our elections, I might find these photographs considerably less offensive.
But they didn't.
We spent four years working our asses off to put this administration in office. We weren't collecting invitations or documenting every fabulous moment of our political lives. We brought humility and hard work. We expected the same from the people entrusted with governing.
Instead, some of these social-media accounts look like society pages.
**Your invitation is not a legislative victory. Your proximity to the president is not an accomplishment. And your seat on Air Force One means absolutely nothing to the family calculating whether it can afford another tank of gas.**
President Trump built his political movement around the idea that Washington had forgotten ordinary Americans. His own White House should be the last place projecting the image of a privileged social club.
I'm not asking anyone to live like a monk. I'm asking for some restraint, some humility, and an appreciation for what Americans endured to put you there.
Spare me another photograph of your fabulous life.
Show me the results.
**We didn 't fight four years so you could spend two years celebrating how wonderful it is to be in Washington.**
**PolitiBrawl is a reader-supported publication. To receive new posts and support our work, please consider becoming a paid subscriber.**

**Texas. Are You Kidding Me?**
Texas.
James Talarico defeated Ken Paxton. Gina Hinojosa defeated Greg Abbott. Democrats swept the statewide offices, ending more than three decades of Republican dominance.
**Every major statewide office. In Texas.**
I'm sorry, but I am not swallowing that without a very serious examination of the numbers.
I find the magnitude of this reversal statistically implausible. That's my opinion, and I want the mathematics examined, not another political consultant explaining that Americans suddenly changed their minds.
Show me the county-by-county returns. Show me the historical comparisons, turnout changes, registration figures, and voting-method breakdowns. Show me how the reported shifts occurred across the state and whether the numbers withstand rigorous independent scrutiny.
I'm not interested in being told that something is possible merely because it happened in the reported results. I want to understand precisely how it happened.
A statistical surprise is not, by itself, proof of misconduct. But the scale of this result warrants serious examination, and I am entitled to question it.
**Texas didn 't just lose a Republican race. Republicans lost the entire statewide political structure they had controlled for more than thirty years.**
Where the hell was Republican leadership?
What did Abbott know? What did Paxton know? What did the polling show? What warnings were ignored? And where was the national party while this was unfolding?
If the results reflect a genuine political realignment, Republicans have an extraordinary failure to explain. If there were election-administration irregularities, those deserve documented investigation.
Either way, somebody owes the American people an accounting.
And I want more than another fundraising email telling me how important the next election will be.
**You had Texas. You lost Texas. Now explain it.**
**We Are Not Your Damn Campaign Staff.**
Washington seems to have forgotten who works for whom.
The Americans who showed up in 2024 weren't auditioning for a fan club. We were citizens who believed the country was in serious trouble. We sacrificed time, money, and peace of mind to elect people we believed would do something about it.
You don't get to demand loyalty and then treat questions as disloyalty. You don't get to campaign on the urgency of saving the country and govern as though time is unlimited. And you don't get to confuse holding office with accomplishing something.
The people who fought hardest to elect you have every right to ask what happened.
**Stop Asking for Applause. Start Answering Questions.**
I've had enough of the slogans, the excuses, and the assumption that supporting Donald Trump requires me to applaud everything his administration and congressional Republicans do.
I supported Trump because I believed he could accomplish what career politicians couldn't. I still believe he has extraordinary abilities. But those abilities don't exempt his administration from scrutiny, and they certainly don't excuse Republican leadership from doing its job.
The people who fought for this victory weren't looking for invitations, recognition, or a front-row seat to Washington's social life. We expected results.
And when the results fall short, we expect accountability.
In the private sector, management doesn't get to miss its objectives, retain the same leadership, celebrate its accomplishments, and then ask the shareholders to trust it for another two years.
Yet somehow Washington considers that business as usual.
**Four years of fighting to win in 2024. Two years for Republicans to deliver.**
And now we're supposed to watch the same people congratulate themselves, blame everyone else, and start campaigning for the next election?
Not a chance.
**We did our part.**
**Where the hell were you when it was time to do yours?**

Support PolitiBrawl by becoming a paid subscriber today: We fought four years to win in 2024. Republicans had two years to deliver. What the hell happened? I am spitting nails. For four years after 2020, Americans paid a price for their political convictions. Families fractured. Friendships ended. Careers and reputations were destroyed. People faced prosecution, imprisonment, financial ruin, and public humiliation. January 6 defendants and their families endured years of legal battles, separation, and financial hardship. Some defendants died by suicide. Whatever anyone thinks about January 6, those families suffered consequences no election victory could erase. We organized, volunteered, donated, knocked on doors, defended our convictions, and showed up at the polls. By 2024 we were exhausted, but we weren't about to quit. We were told to make the election too big to rig , and we did everything within our power to deliver. We weren't expecting miracles. We knew the mess was enormous and that Washington would fight every inch. What I never imagined was that two years later I would still be wondering whether the Republicans we elected had the slightest appreciation for what it took to put them in office. Four years of absolute hell to win in 2024, and Republicans managed to squander the opportunity in two. How the hell did we get here? I was a registered Independent until Donald Trump came along. I've never had much use for career politicians who promise to fix problems, become part of the problem, and then run again on the same promises. In the private sector that record gets you fired. In Washington it gets you a leadership post and a standing ovation. These people couldn 't run a lemonade stand, but they think they're qualified to run the country. Trump appealed because he wasn't one of them. He was a builder and a negotiator. I never bought the claim that he is stupid. You don't build that kind of business record by being the bumbling idiot his critics need him to be. I've said it many times: Trump is playing world-class chess while the left is playing checkers. Which makes the 2026 midterms all the more maddening. PolitiBrawl is a reader-supported publication. To receive new posts and support our work, please consider becoming a paid subscriber. If Trump is playing world-class chess, how in God's name did Republicans lose the board? I didn't expect him to personally manage Congress. I did expect him to recognize the people who couldn't execute, deal with them, and make certain his administration wasn't wasting the opportunity Americans fought four years to give him. Trump knows better than anyone that a brilliant strategy is worthless if the people responsible for executing it can't deliver. So I have questions for him, too. When did he recognize that congressional leadership wasn't getting the job done? What did he do about it? And why did Republicans reach November with priorities still unfinished? I have defended Trump's intelligence for years. I'm not about to insult it now by pretending he bears no responsibility for the people and decisions surrounding his administration. If you 're playing world-class chess, you had better know who's moving your pieces. What Exactly Did Republicans Do With the Opportunity We Gave Them? I spent years on business turnarounds. When a company is in trouble you don't get paid for explaining why the deal didn't close. You get paid to close it. Republicans knew the Senate rules, the margins, the opposition, and the date of the next election. None of this was a surprise. So why did so much remain unfinished? Explain what the plan was to overcome the obstacles. Explain what was tried, what failed, and why the strategy wasn't changed when time started running out. After everything Trump and his supporters went through with the old establishment, Senate Republicans chose John Thune--a longtime member of Mitch McConnell's leadership orbit--over Rick Scott. Scott was eliminated in the first round. After the 2026 losses they reelected Thune unopposed. We 're not giving up this fight, and neither should you The midterms were a wake up call to all American patriots... | | ---|---|--- The battle ahead will surely be hard and up-hill. But think of the brave Americans who stormed the beaches of Normandy, or the men who fought and bled at Shiloh and Lexington. They had a dream for America they were willing to die for. We cannot let their sacrifice be in vain. This is what we believe in. We must fight for our nation with everything we've got, even on the darkest days, as our ancestors did. PolitiBrawl will hold our place in line on the battleground for information and news. We appreciate your readership and support. Do not give up hope. Tomorrow is a brighter day. (Piece continues): You cannot make this stuff up. Speaker Mike Johnson has said nearly 700 House-passed measures were awaiting Senate action. Not every bill is a priority, but the backlog raises the obvious question about what Senate leadership was doing with the limited time it had. On nominations, as of November 12 there were still 195 civilian nominations awaiting Senate action, 157 of which had not cleared committee. The Senate confirmed hundreds and changed some procedures to speed things up. An administration still needs its people in place. That isn't complicated. In what other profession does management preside over a disaster and get rewarded with another term? Only in Washington. Six Years of Election-Integrity Concerns. And We Still Didn 't Get It Done. This one absolutely infuriates me. Americans have been arguing about voter rolls, identification, citizenship verification, and election administration since 2020. Six years of controversy and declining confidence among a large share of the electorate. The House passed the SAVE Act in April 2025 and the SAVE America Act in February 2026. Neither became law before the midterms. Republicans knew the opposition and the Senate's rules. If the votes weren't there, what alternatives were considered? If leadership concluded it couldn't pass, why wasn't that explained to the people who had been told for years that this was essential? I am not interested in another fundraising email about election integrity. I want the explanation for why Republicans entered the 2026 midterms without it. And now, with Democrats taking control of Congress, how exactly do they propose to get it done? Enough With the Damn Parties and Air Force One Selfies. | | ---|---|--- To the people inside the Trump White House: read the damn room. I open social media and there it is again. Another fabulous reception. Another glamorous dinner. Another Air Force One selfie. Another VIP experience accompanied by a breathless post about what an extraordinary privilege it is to be there. We get it. You're having the time of your lives. Americans are standing at gas pumps, paying outrageous insurance premiums, and trying to figure out how their grocery bills got so high. Republicans just suffered a political disaster. Election-integrity legislation never made it across the finish line. And the White House social scene appears to be thriving. What exactly are we celebrating? I understand the excitement of working in the White House. But the relentless boasting is becoming revolting when the priorities Americans were told were urgent remain unfinished. If Republicans had delivered on their promises, starting with securing our elections, I might find these photographs considerably less offensive. But they didn't. We spent four years working our asses off to put this administration in office. We weren't collecting invitations or documenting every fabulous moment of our political lives. We brought humility and hard work. We expected the same from the people entrusted with governing. Instead, some of these social-media accounts look like society pages. Your invitation is not a legislative victory. Your proximity to the president is not an accomplishment. And your seat on Air Force One means absolutely nothing to the family calculating whether it can afford another tank of gas. President Trump built his political movement around the idea that Washington had forgotten ordinary Americans. His own White House should be the last place projecting the image of a privileged social club. I'm not asking anyone to live like a monk. I'm asking for some restraint, some humility, and an appreciation for what Americans endured to put you there. Spare me another photograph of your fabulous life. Show me the results. We didn 't fight four years so you could spend two years celebrating how wonderful it is to be in Washington. PolitiBrawl is a reader-supported publication. To receive new posts and support our work, please consider becoming a paid subscriber. Texas. Are You Kidding Me? Texas. James Talarico defeated Ken Paxton. Gina Hinojosa defeated Greg Abbott. Democrats swept the statewide offices, ending more than three decades of Republican dominance. Every major statewide office. In Texas. I'm sorry, but I am not swallowing that without a very serious examination of the numbers. I find the magnitude of this reversal statistically implausible. That's my opinion, and I want the mathematics examined, not another political consultant explaining that Americans suddenly changed their minds. Show me the county-by-county returns. Show me the historical comparisons, turnout changes, registration figures, and voting-method breakdowns. Show me how the reported shifts occurred across the state and whether the numbers withstand rigorous independent scrutiny. I'm not interested in being told that something is possible merely because it happened in the reported results. I want to understand precisely how it happened. A statistical surprise is not, by itself, proof of misconduct. But the scale of this result warrants serious examination, and I am entitled to question it. Texas didn 't just lose a Republican race. Republicans lost the entire statewide political structure they had controlled for more than thirty years. Where the hell was Republican leadership? What did Abbott know? What did Paxton know? What did the polling show? What warnings were ignored? And where was the national party while this was unfolding? If the results reflect a genuine political realignment, Republicans have an extraordinary failure to explain. If there were election-administration irregularities, those deserve documented investigation. Either way, somebody owes the American people an accounting. And I want more than another fundraising email telling me how important the next election will be. You had Texas. You lost Texas. Now explain it. We Are Not Your Damn Campaign Staff. Washington seems to have forgotten who works for whom. The Americans who showed up in 2024 weren't auditioning for a fan club. We were citizens who believed the country was in serious trouble. We sacrificed time, money, and peace of mind to elect people we believed would do something about it. You don't get to demand loyalty and then treat questions as disloyalty. You don't get to campaign on the urgency of saving the country and govern as though time is unlimited. And you don't get to confuse holding office with accomplishing something. The people who fought hardest to elect you have every right to ask what happened. Stop Asking for Applause. Start Answering Questions. I've had enough of the slogans, the excuses, and the assumption that supporting Donald Trump requires me to applaud everything his administration and congressional Republicans do. I supported Trump because I believed he could accomplish what career politicians couldn't. I still believe he has extraordinary abilities. But those abilities don't exempt his administration from scrutiny, and they certainly don't excuse Republican leadership from doing its job. The people who fought for this victory weren't looking for invitations, recognition, or a front-row seat to Washington's social life. We expected results. And when the results fall short, we expect accountability. In the private sector, management doesn't get to miss its objectives, retain the same leadership, celebrate its accomplishments, and then ask the shareholders to trust it for another two years. Yet somehow Washington considers that business as usual. Four years of fighting to win in 2024. Two years for Republicans to deliver. And now we're supposed to watch the same people congratulate themselves, blame everyone else, and start campaigning for the next election? Not a chance. We did our part. Where the hell were you when it was time to do yours? About the Author Wendy M. body:
Continuing an era of change.
# [](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/852?refcode=em20261113-1&t=1&akid=4245%2E587540%2Ev4r0DV)
[](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/sign/lwd-em20261113-schumer/?source=em20261113-4245&t=2&akid=4245%2E587540%2Ev4r0DV)
Peter, we just saw a tsunami of people across the country decide they were ready for a change in leadership.
So why are we drawing the line at Democratic Party leadership? In answering the question “ _what comes next?_ ” after an indisputable “change election” in the midterms, the response from the establishment is to...keep the same leadership.
Chuck Schumer is currently the Senate Minority Leader and he’s aiming to become the Majority Leader (again) in the next Congress.
But he has shown that he can’t meet the moment and fight for policies that the American people actually want to see. He has failed to address major issues facing us currently — such as income inequality, the rapid expansion of AI, and more — and he’s been too soft on Republican initiatives and corruption.
It’s uninspiring to see this massive shift towards younger, more progressive leaders _just to stick with a party leader who has been in the Senate for nearly 30 years, and in federal office for over 45 years_.
This is our chance to give new leaders a platform. We need a new, bold voice in the Senate to stand up to Trump and his corrupt administration and to _actually get things done for working people_.
**Change starts with you, Peter. We won’t see change unless we make it.** It’s time for a new Senate Majority Leader, and we need to put pressure on sitting and newly-elected senators to hear our calls for change.
**[It’s time for change. Add your name now to oppose Chuck Schumer as Majority Leader.](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/sign/lwd-em20261113-schumer/?source=em20261113-4245&t=3&akid=4245%2E587540%2Ev4r0DV)**

David Hogg

November 13, 2026
**Contact: **Duane Dichiara
Email: Ddichiara@axiomstrategies.com
---
| | **Alexandra Duarte Declares Victory in Senate District 4**
---
| **SACRAMENTO** — Alexandra Duarte has declared victory in the race for California’s 4th State Senate District, defeating Tuolumne County Supervisor Jaron Brandon by nearly 16,000 votes, representing the largest win for any Republican in a battleground district in California.

Duarte is a conservative farmer and mom who lives with her family on a ranch in Stanislaus County.

_“Thank you to the voters of the Sierra and the Central Valley for trusting me to represent you,”_ said **Duarte**. _“To every volunteer, every donor, my campaign team and my family: we did this together.”_

_“In a tough year for Republicans, we defied the trend,”_ said **Duarte**._“We won by taking conservative values into every community in this district, by listening to people who’d been ignored for years, and by telling them the truth: they deserve better than what Sacramento gives them, and we can change it. In a year when so many conservative voters stayed home, we gave them a reason to show up. And they did.”_

Duarte thanked Supervisor Brandon for his service and his campaign. _“I congratulate Supervisor Brandon on a hard-fought race and thank him for his six years of service to Tuolumne County. I look forward to working with him to serve our community.”

“I’m ready to get to work.” _

body:

| [](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_su_pros_jtk1747&source=&t=1&akid=5354%2E124072%2EdhQXe_) | | | |

We did it, Peter! 🎉
Democrats pulled off some historic upsets in this year’s midterm elections, held crucial battleground seats and took back the Senate majority. Soon, Roy Cooper will be sworn in as North Carolina’s next U.S. Senator – the first Democratic Senator elected from our state in nearly two decades.
Roy is ready to fix what’s broken in Washington DC. He’s ready to _make stuff cost less_ and be a champion for working families across the country. He won’t stop fighting for us, and we want to show him this team has his back.
**That’s why we’re putting together a congratulations card for the Senator-elect, and we’re counting on 25,000 folks to sign it today – including you, Peter.**
**_[Will you sign the card congratulating Roy and wish him well before he heads to Washington DC? We know he’ll appreciate it, and we can’t wait to show him all of the people cheering him on!](https://act.roycooper.com/survey/sign-the-card-2026-email/?email=&zip=&amounts=5,25,50,100,250&ask=5&source=email_su_pros_jtk1747&t=3&akid=5354%2E124072%2EdhQXe_)_**

name: Pramila Jayapal
subject: I keep getting asked this question
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Pramila for Congress
body:
Affordability and accountability are two sides of the same coin.
# [](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/892?refcode=em20261113-6957-footer&t=1&akid=6957%2E420207%2ES4AvgP)
Peter,
I was on MSNow this week, and I got a question I’ve been hearing a lot lately: now that Democrats have the majority, what should we focus on first — fighting for working people or holding the Trump administration accountable?
My answer: **We have to do both.**
Affordability and accountability aren’t two separate fights. _They’re two sides of the same coin._
Working people are struggling right now to afford a full tank of gas, food on the table, and healthcare for their families. _Why?_
**Because Trump has orchestrated one of the largest transfers of wealth in our history, from everyday Americans straight into the pockets of the ulra-rich.**
While families stretch every dollar to make it to the next week, Trump pours millions into a ballroom, takes over the Kennedy Center, and enriches himself and his allies.
It’s corruption, plain and simple. _And it’s making your life more expensive._
So yes, we absolutely have to deliver for people in ways they will feel in their daily budgets. Lower prices at the pump and the grocery store, wages you can actually live on, and a doctor’s visit without going broke. AND we have to hold this administration accountable, because **the corruption IS the cost.**
If we fix what’s broken without holding their feet to the fire, they’ll find new ways to rig the system and working families will pay the price — _again._
Voters across the country gave us this majority because they want both. A government that makes life more affordable, and one that refuses to let the powerful get away with abusing their authority. That’s exactly what I’m fighting for.
[**But I can’t take on this fight alone. If you can, please pitch in $3 to help me fight for affordability and accountability on Day 1 and every day after.**](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-em-20261113-1.O-BjIP&refcode=em20261113-6957&amount=3&t=2&akid=6957%2E420207%2ES4AvgP)

In solidarity,

name: America Fitzpatrick, LCV
subject: TAKE ACTION: Hands Off the Arctic Refuge!
body:
To view this mail in a browser, copy https://links.messages.lcv.org/servlet/MailView?ms=MTQwOTUwNzkS1&r=NjA3MDU0MTAzNTc3S0&j=MjU4MDA3MDM5NgS2&mt=1&rt=0 into your browser.
Hands Off the Arctic Refuge — Speak Out Against Seismic Testing for Oil!

In the final weeks before the new Congress is seated, the Trump administration
is doing everything it can to push forward oil development in the irreplaceable
Arctic National Wildlife Refuge. The administration is now moving to advance
harmful seismic testing, the first step in oil development, that could destroy polar bear dens and habitat, scar the fragile tundra, and jeopardize
Indigenous lifeways and subsistence traditions.

The Gwich’in people are the original stewards of the Arctic Refuge, and LCV
continues to stand with them in this fight. We’re calling on people across the
country to take action to block seismic testing and protect one of our country’s
last wild places.

Tell Secretary Burgum: No Seismic Testing in the Arctic Refuge! https://links.messages.lcv.org/els/v2/EZ_ ADD YOUR NAME https://links.messages.lcv. Peter, In the final weeks before the new Congress is seated, the Trump administration
is moving to advance oil development in the Arctic National Wildlife Refuge’s
culturally and ecologically critical Coastal Plain — beginning with harmful
seismic testing. Seismic testing is the first step in oil development and requires massive
trucks, some as heavy as 90,000 pounds, to pound the fragile Arctic tundra with
powerful vibrations to search for oil. Seismic testing destroys essential habitats and leaves deep scars on the
landscape that last for decades. The noise and activity generated during testing
disrupt wildlife migrations, causing fear and confusion that can lead animal
mothers to abandon their young. On top of this, the Arctic Refuge is already facing the cumulative impact of
climate change and environmental and wildlife protection rollbacks. Among the
most damaging rollbacks is the administration's change to the definition of
"harm" under the Endangered Species Act, which revoked significant protections
for polar bears and other species. The change means that if seismic testing
crushes polar bear dens, destroying their homes and threatening their lives,
there will be no repercussions for Big Oil. Add your voice today: hands off the Arctic Refuge >> https://links.messages.lcv.org/els/v2/x_yzTg8a~ TAKE ACTION NOW https://links.messages.lcv.org/els/v2/KybpT- We cannot let Trump and his Big Oil cronies destroy the irreplaceable Arctic
Refuge in pursuit of dirty energy development. For decades, the Gwich'in people
have led the movement to keep the Arctic Refuge free from corporate greed and
extraction — no drilling, no development. LCV stands with the Gwich’in people and opposes seismic testing on these sacred
lands, and in the entire region. There are lasting consequences to pursuing oil
development in this region — even before any drilling starts — that could have
disastrous outcomes for Indigenous communities, wildlife, and our climate. Nothing justifies developing one of the last wild places on earth. Join LCV in sending a clear message to protect the Arctic Refuge: no seismic testing! https://links.messages.lcv. Thank you for standing with LCV and with all the protectors of the Arctic
Refuge, so that this irreplaceable landscape may continue to thrive for future
generations. America Fitzpatrick
Conservation Program Director
League of Conservation Voters This email was sent to dpwillis67@gmail.com.
